item.title: Serie A Preview: Venezia vs Inter – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
item.description: Serie A Preview: Venezia vs Inter – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Wednesday’s Serie A clash between Venezia and Inter has all the makings of a ‘David vs Goliath’ contest as the division’s last side encounters the high-flying reigning champions. The teams head into proceedings in starkly contrasting spirits after the weekend. Despite beating Napoli 1-0 in their last home outing, Venezia failed to build on their first win of the season as they found themselves on the receiving end of the same scoreline away to Genoa on Saturday. New manager Davide Nicola may have won on his touchline debut, but steering the Winged Lions away from the foot of the table could prove a Herculean task. Except for that shocking victory over Napoli, Venezia have lost all seven remaining league fixtures this season. However, they commence this midweek round only a point adrift of 17th-placed Udinese, meaning another unlikely win here could lift them out of the bottom three. Unlike their out-of-sorts hosts, Inter enjoyed another successful weekend. Serie A’s ‘comeback specialists’ lived up to their reputation on Sunday, with stoppage-time goals from Marcus Thuram and Piotr Zielinski propelling them to a come-from-behind 2-1 win over Fiorentina. There’s no room for complacency at San Siro, even though Cristian Chivu’s men sit at the table’s summit heading into this matchday. Sitting above Lazio on goal difference alone, the Nerazzurri can ill-afford a slip-up at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo if they’re to stay there before next weekend’s Milan derby. Match Preview Venezia Nicola’s winning start quickly faded away as Venezia slumped to their eight defeat in nine competitive matches this term (W1), failing to get on the scoresheet for the second time in their last four. In addition to their well-documented scoring woes, the Winged Lions have been notoriously prone to conceding in abundance, capitulating at least twice in seven of those eight losses. Against this backdrop, Venezia have been relatively solid at the back when playing on home turf, conceding one goal or fewer in 11 of their last 16 Serie A outings at the Pier Luigi Penzo. After beating Napoli in their most recent game here, they could win back-to-back top-flight home matches to nil for the first time since 1967. However, Venezia’s upcoming opponent cannot be more formidable. Since their last competitive win over Inter back in October 1999, Venezia have managed just one draw in eight meetings with the Nerazzurri (L7), losing the last five in a row by an aggregate score of 11-2. Except for a 2-2 draw at Roma last month, Chivu’s charges have won their remaining four league fixtures when conceding the opening goal, meaning it’s impossible to write them off at any point. item.content:encoded: Serie A Preview: Venezia vs Inter – Team News, Lineups & Prediction Wednesday’s Serie A clash between Venezia and Inter has all the makings of a ‘David vs Goliath’ contest as the division’s last side encounters the high-flying reigning champions. The teams head into proceedings in starkly contrasting spirits after the weekend. Despite beating Napoli 1-0 in their last home outing, Venezia failed to build on their first win of the season as they found themselves on the receiving end of the same scoreline away to Genoa on Saturday. New manager Davide Nicola may have won on his touchline debut, but steering the Winged Lions away from the foot of the table could prove a Herculean task. Except for that shocking victory over Napoli, Venezia have lost all seven remaining league fixtures this season. However, they commence this midweek round only a point adrift of 17th-placed Udinese, meaning another unlikely win here could lift them out of the bottom three. Unlike their out-of-sorts hosts, Inter enjoyed another successful weekend. Serie A’s ‘comeback specialists’ lived up to their reputation on Sunday, with stoppage-time goals from Marcus Thuram and Piotr Zielinski propelling them to a come-from-behind 2-1 win over Fiorentina. There’s no room for complacency at San Siro, even though Cristian Chivu’s men sit at the table’s summit heading into this matchday. Sitting above Lazio on goal difference alone, the Nerazzurri can ill-afford a slip-up at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo if they’re to stay there before next weekend’s Milan derby. Match Preview Venezia Nicola’s winning start quickly faded away as Venezia slumped to their eight defeat in nine competitive matches this term (W1), failing to get on the scoresheet for the second time in their last four. In addition to their well-documented scoring woes, the Winged Lions have been notoriously prone to conceding in abundance, capitulating at least twice in seven of those eight losses. Against this backdrop, Venezia have been relatively solid at the back when playing on home turf, conceding one goal or fewer in 11 of their last 16 Serie A outings at the Pier Luigi Penzo. After beating Napoli in their most recent game here, they could win back-to-back top-flight home matches to nil for the first time since 1967. However, Venezia’s upcoming opponent cannot be more formidable. Since their last competitive win over Inter back in October 1999, Venezia have managed just one draw in eight meetings with the Nerazzurri (L7), losing the last five in a row by an aggregate score of 11-2. Inter Inter once again demonstrated their unrivaled fighting spirit last weekend, as they’ve now won a whopping 13 points from losing positions this season! Except for a 2-2 draw at Roma last month, Chivu’s charges have won their remaining four league fixtures when conceding the opening goal, meaning it’s impossible to write them off at any point. That’s largely thanks to their free-firing frontline that’s bagged a league-high 23 goals, at least four more than any other side in the division. Given Venezia’s current situation, this should be a walk in the park for the Nerazzurri, who are chasing four consecutive wins in all competitions for the first time this season. Yet, the defending champions would be well-advised not to take anything for granted, considering their recent slump on the road. Indeed, Inter have won just two of their last five away matches (D2, L1), keeping just one clean sheet during that sequence. Team New Venezia boss Nicola cannot call upon Marin Sverko, Bartol Franjic, and Andrea Adorante for this high-stakes fixture, while wingback Thierry Correia remains a fitness doubt. All eyes will be on the club’s record signing, Akor Adams, who has tallied two goals in his last four appearances. On the other hand, Inter will take this trip without long-term absentees John Stones, Curtis Jones, and Benjamin Pavard. Luis Henrique and Lautaro Martinez are also on the sidelines, with Francesco Pio Espostio expected to take the latter’s place in attack and partner up with Thuram. Venezia vs Inter Potential Starting Lineups Venezia (3-5-2): F. Stankovic; Schingtienne, Halhal, Moreno; Hainaut, Perez, Basic, Sohm, Haps; Yeboah, Adams. Inter (3-5-2): J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Augusto; Spence, Sucic, A. Stankovic, Zielinski, Dimarco; Bonny, Esposito. Venezia vs Inter Prediction It would take a ‘once in a lifetime’ miracle for Venezia to knock Inter off their perch, with the Nerazzurri set to take the field amid their best Serie A start since 2017. Although the hosts desperately need to catch a break, this should be another day in the office for Chivu’s high-performing side.

item.title: Inter Milan XI vs Venezia – Predicted lineup and team news
item.description: Inter Milan XI vs Venezia – Predicted lineup and team news Inter Milan will aim to stay at the summit of Serie A when they visit Venezia for their next league fixture on Wednesday. The defending champions come into the match in outstanding shape, still unbeaten in the league after seven victories and one draw. Inter possess the division’s strongest attack, having scored 23 goals, and Cristian Chivu’s side have claimed wins in four of their previous five games in all competitions. They returned to first place in dramatic style last weekend, coming from behind to beat Fiorentina 2-1 thanks to Piotr Zielinski’s stoppage-time strike in the 98th minute. Inter Milan team news Lautaro Martinez is definitely unavailable after picking up a hamstring injury during the match against Club Brugge, creating a major gap in Inter’s forward line. Chivu is also short of options at the back and in midfield, with Benjamin Pavard, John Stones, and Curtis Jones all ruled out as they work their way back to full fitness. Wing-back Luis Henrique will be sidelined until the November international break because of an adductor strain. With rotation expected to preserve the fitness of key players, Marcus Thuram may be left on the substitutes’ bench. That could give young attackers Pio Esposito and Ange Bonny the chance to lead the line in a heavily changed 3-5-2 formation, as Inter continue their pursuit of another Serie A title. Inter Milan predicted lineup Possible Inter Milan starting XI: J. Martinez; Bisseck, Akanji, Augusto; Spence, Sucic, A. Stankovic, Zielinski, Dimarco; Bonny, Esposito When will the match kick off? The match will kick off at 5:30pm BST on Wednesday, 28th October. How to watch Venezia vs Inter Milan? Viewers in the UK can follow the Venezia versus Inter Milan game live on DAZN. item.title: “Fundamentally Poor”: Rick Pitino Makes Honest Assessment of St. John’s Preseason Games
item.description: Oct 1, 2026; New York, NY, USA; St. John's Red Storm head coach Rick Pitino speaks at 2026 Big East Media Day at Marriott Marquis. © Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Rick Pitino’s St. John’s go into the new season after an undefeated 3-0 preseason. They faced Drexel, Rutgers and No. 7 Texas in the three exhibition games. St. John’s won 104-99 in a four-overtime thriller against Rutgers on Oct. 18. After the game, Pitino said that if they play like that against the Longhorns, they’d lose by 40 points. Broadcaster John Fanta asked Pitino about that comment and how he would rate the 87-74 win over Texas on Sunday. Pitino talked about the new-look team. “We have 11 new players, and we lost Zuby (Eljofor), who was the heart and soul of our basketball team, along with two other draft choices, Bryce Hopkins and Dillon Mitchell. We have a good, talented basketball team, but they’re fundamentally very poor,” Pitino said . “First of all, if you listen to a word I say in preseason in trying to get my team up for things, you’d be foolish because nothing I say is relevant or the truth. Rutgers has played extremely well. They’re a good basketball team, much better than people think,” he said about his comments after the Rutgers game. Rick Pitino grades St. John’s preseason games Despite a perfect preseason record, Pitino wasn’t overly impressed with his team. He believes his players have a long way to go and need to improve a lot. “I graded out. (On) my grading system, a C-minus. Now, Rutgers was an F and Drexel was a D. And to be perfectly honest with you, this time of year, you’re probably going to grade your team a C or a C-plus. If you’re in B, you’ve got yourself a really special team,” he said. item.title: Runners swap streets for shopping malls as haze chokes Singapore
item.description: Fitness enthusiasts run inside a Singapore mall (Roslan RAHMAN) The pounding of running shoes echoes through a Singapore shopping mall as fitness enthusiasts desperate to exercise take refuge from choking haze. Smoke from wildfires in neighbouring Indonesia has sent air quality in the city-state plummeting to its worst levels in more than a decade in recent weeks, cancelling outdoor activities. Those seeking exercise, including runners training for international events, have found an unconventional alternative: air-conditioned shopping malls. On Saturday more than 80 runners turned the corridors of Marina Square shopping centre into makeshift running tracks, clocking laps past storefronts on two floors before shops opened for business. There are strict rules. "No sprinting, no overtaking, no shouting or yelling," Eugene Beh, 52, founder of Singapore Runners Club, told about 60 members before their run. Spitting and wiping sweat on the floor are also banned. Beh said they had to cancel several runs outdoors because of the haze, blown in by the wind from forest and peatland fires in Borneo and Sumatra. - 'Very mental' - Angeline Zeng, 57, who works in banking, completed 10 loops at the mall, or about 10 kilometres (six miles). With a half-marathon in Taipei in less than a week and a full marathon in December, Zeng needs to clock as much mileage as she can. Since treadmills at her neighbourhood gym are often full, she and her fellow runners were excited when they heard about the mall runs. "We were like, wow, we didn't expect that at all," she told AFP. "I love it because the aircon makes you feel like you're running overseas where there's cold temperatures, so it's really great," Zeng added. But she said that circling inside the mall becomes "boring" after a while. "Maybe for shorter runs this is okay but if you need to do long runs, maybe not so suitable," she said. Singapore Runners Club member Doris Tan, 42, said she thought running indoors would be a bit suffocating. "I didn't expect it to be so cool... but if you have to ask me, I still prefer outdoors," she told AFP. Paul Wong, a 54-year-old retiree from a club called X-Run, completed 21 loops inside the mall, or about 21 km. With just over a month until the Singapore International Marathon -– which many other fellow runners are also training for -– Wong would have to run up to 80 km per week, but the haze has forced him indoors. "For the last two weeks I've been running close to 100 kilometres on the treadmill. The longest I've run is 28 km for two and a half hours, it's very mental," Wong said. "The mall run is definitely better because the treadmill feels like a hamster run. You just keep repeating the routine." Eddie Chang, lead coach for X-Run, said they had to present a carefully laid-out plan to get approval from the mall for the runs. But she said that circling inside the mall becomes "boring" after a while. "Maybe for shorter runs this is okay but if you need to do long runs, maybe not so suitable," she said. Singapore Runners Club member Doris Tan, 42, said she thought running indoors would be a bit suffocating. "I didn't expect it to be so cool... but if you have to ask me, I still prefer outdoors," she told AFP. Paul Wong, a 54-year-old retiree from a club called X-Run, completed 21 loops inside the mall, or about 21 km. "The mall run is definitely better because the treadmill feels like a hamster run. You just keep repeating the routine." Eddie Chang, lead coach for X-Run, said they had to present a carefully laid-out plan to get approval from the mall for the runs. They had to consider factors like walkway width, tight corners and holding the run early in the morning before the shops open. - Just the start? - "The biggest challenge for outdoor training is the weather. Humidity is very high, plus the haze now, the impact is doubled and tripled, so it's very hard to manage," Chang told AFP. "By converting to indoors, you definitely reduce all the impact from the outdoor experience and continue running." The air quality improved this week but on Wednesday Singapore remained one of the 20 most polluted major cities in the world, according to Swiss-based air quality monitor IQAir. The two running clubs are likely to extend the mall runs if poor air quality persists, and plan to ask more malls to open their doors to them. "I believe there will be opportunities. This is something new in the sports scene," Beh said. "Hopefully, with the permission of building management, this can spread out to other sports groups." str/jhe

item.title: Venezia vs Inter Milan – Match preview and team news
item.description: Venezia vs Inter Milan – Match preview and team news Inter Milan will hope to retain the top spot in the Serie A table by securing all three points while travelling to face Venezia in their next league game on Wednesday . Venezia vs Inter Milan – Match preview and team news Date: Wednesday, 28th October. Kick-off: 5:30pm BST. Venue: Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo, Venezia. Venezia team news Venezia manager Davide Nicola faces a tough task reshaping his squad as they prepare to host the reigning champions at the Penzo. The primary boost for the relegation-threatened side is the highly anticipated return of captain Gianluca Busio, who has fully recovered from a thigh injury and could force his way straight back into the starting lineup. However, the Lagunari remain heavily depleted in other areas, with Marin Sverko, Bartol Franjic, and Andrea Adorante all officially ruled out of the matchday squad. Adding to Nicola’s defensive worries, wing-back Thierry Correia remains a major late fitness doubt with a persistent thigh issue and will undergo close monitoring right up until kick-off. Venezia are expected to deploy a defensive 3-5-2 system, likely relying on a frontline of John Yeboah and Akor Adams to breach Inter’s backline. Inter Milan team news Captain Lautaro Martinez remains completely sidelined following a hamstring injury suffered against Club Brugge, leaving a massive void in the Nerazzurri attack. Cristian Chivu’s defensive and midfield options are also severely restricted, with Benjamin Pavard, John Stones, and Curtis Jones all confirmed absentees as they struggle to regain full match fitness. Additionally, wing-back Luis Henrique is out until the November international break due to an adductor strain. With squad rotation highly anticipated to keep key players fresh, star forward Marcus Thuram could be rested on the bench. This opens the door for young strikers Pio Esposito and Ange Bonny to spearhead the attack in a heavily rotated 3-5-2 system as Inter look to maintain their Scudetto defence. Form Venezia Venezia are enduring a dismal return to the top flight, sitting rock bottom of Serie A with just three points. The Lagunari have suffered seven defeats in their opening eight league games, conceding at an alarming rate of over two goals per match. While new manager Davide Nicola sparked temporary hope with a stunning 1-0 upset over Napoli, that momentum evaporated immediately following a disappointing 1-0 defeat to Genoa last weekend. Inter Milan Reigning champions Inter Milan arrive in sensational form, remaining unbeaten in Serie A with seven wins and one draw. Boasting the league’s most prolific attack with 23 goals, Cristian Chivu’s men have won four of their last five matches across all competitions. They reclaimed the top spot in dramatic fashion last weekend, sealing a thrilling -2-1 comeback victory against Fiorentina courtesy of a ninety-eighth-minute winner from Piotr Zielinski. item.title: Jayson Tatum sends NBA warning after game-winning buzzer beater in Celtics win
item.description: Photo By Winslow Townson/Getty Images Jayson Tatum had a statement performance in the Boston Celtics’ win against the Brooklyn Nets, and he had a message for everyone after. All the talk recently surrounding Jayson Tatum has been about his relationship with his former co-star Jaylen Brown. The two have been going back and forth a bit after games, but the focus has been firmly away from what is happening on the floor. Tatum’s recent performance has brought the attention right back. In Tuesday night’s clash against the Brooklyn Nets, he had a whopping 40 points during the game. JT also iced the game in overtime with a buzzer beater that ended up winning the game for Boston. Jayson Tatum says he is ‘feeling like himself’ after Celtics win Tatum has been discussed quite a bit recently, and many fans and analysts have suggested that he might not be able to get back to his best after his injury. Since he returned towards the end of last season, JT hasn’t quite looked like his dominant self either, lending further credence to those takes. However, as they say in sports, class is permanent. And the 28-year-old has sent a message to the rest of the league, which they should take as a warning. “I’m starting to feel like my old self,” Tatum said after the game. Considering that his old self has been named to the All-NBA First Team four times, it should worry the Eastern Conference if JT is getting his confidence back. The Celtics star had 40 points, five rebounds, and eight assists against Brooklyn. All the talk recently surrounding Jayson Tatum has been about his relationship with his former co-star Jaylen Brown. The two have been going back and forth a bit after games, but the focus has been firmly away from what is happening on the floor. Tatum’s recent performance has brought the attention right back. Jayson Tatum says he is ‘feeling like himself’ after Celtics win Tatum has been discussed quite a bit recently, and many fans and analysts have suggested that he might not be able to get back to his best after his injury. item.title: AC Milan vs Bologna – Predicted lineup and team news
item.description: AC Milan vs Bologna – Predicted lineup and team news AC Milan will welcome Bologna to the San Siro on Wednesday as they aim to collect another important set of three points in Serie A under Ruben Amorim. Milan are among just four sides yet to lose in Serie A this campaign, having picked up five victories and three draws from their first eight fixtures. Their domestic form under Amorim has been strong, most recently shown in a composed 2-0 win away at Udinese on Sunday. However, they were dealt a disappointing 3-0 defeat by Bournemouth in the Europa League during the week. Despite that result, Milan have been especially difficult to beat on home soil and remain unbeaten at the San Siro this season. AC Milan team news Amorim has a major team-news headache before tonight’s match, with as many as eight senior players either unavailable or facing fitness doubts. The most significant absence is Ruben Loftus-Cheek, who will be out for roughly a month after injuring his thigh against Udinese. He is joined on the unavailable list by Samuel Chukwueze, Mattia Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Filippo Terracciano. Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira and Mario Gila are also serious doubts after sitting out the weekend match. With a huge derby against Inter Milan scheduled for Saturday, Amorim may choose to manage the workload of the players still available. Luka Modrić is likely to begin the game among the substitutes, while Christian Pulisic may also be used sparingly. Youngster Alphadjo Cissé is strongly expected to come into the starting XI in an attacking role behind striker Gonçalo Ramos. That change could significantly alter Milan’s usual setup. AC Milan predicted lineup Possible AC Milan starting XI: Maignan; Tomori, De Winter, Pavlovic, Bartesaghi; Hutchinson, Jashari, Musah, Cisse; Pulisic, Ramos When will the match kick off? The match will kick off at 5:30pm BST on Wednesday, 28th October. How to watch AC Milan vs Bologna? The match will be shown live on TNT Sports 1. Add The Sporting News as a preferred news source How many players are there in a Hong Kong Sixes team? Each side fields six players, unlike 11 players playing in traditional cricket games. In the tournament squad, extra players can be considered; however, only six players take to the pitch during a match. This shortened version puts the onus on all-rounder players because sides have to maintain a balance of their batting prowess along with their bowlers and fielders. This game has been framed keeping the attacking cricket in mind, where the batters have to run up high scores, while the bowlers have to play their part in the limited overs. MORE: India team for Hong Kong Sixes 2026 How many overs are played in Hong Kong Sixes? Each team get six overs per inning, meaning that there will be 12 total overs in one match, regardless of the number of wides and no balls that cause the addition of more balls in the game. The bowlers usually bowl one over each, but there may be one designated bowler who can bowl two overs. Wicketkeeper is the only player on the team who does not need to bowl. As there are just six overs for the teams to bat, there is little chance for them to build an innings slowly. MORE: Visit Cricket News for all the latest cricket coverage and opinion Which teams are playing in Hong Kong Sixes 2026? The 12 participating teams have been divided into four groups: Group Teams Group A Australia, England, Hong Kong, China Group B Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Scotland Group C India, Pakistan, UAE Group D South Africa, Afghanistan, Oman Pakistan are the defending champions, having won the 2025 tournament. They hope to win their seventh trophy in the history of the tournament. Hong Kong Sixes 2026 tournament format The 2026 edition of the tournament consists of 12 teams split into four groups of three with each team playing the other two teams in their group. The teams will be distributed among three different finals based on their position in the group stages. The group winners will go to the Cup semi-finals while the second-placed teams will be competing in the Plate semi-finals and the third-placed teams will join the Bowl competition. The knock-out games start on October 31 with the finals, with classification matches taking place on November 1. Each of the teams will play throughout the tournament with final classifications from 1st to 12th decided through different tournaments. The tournament will have 25 matches over three days including a women's exhibition match. What are the rules of Hong Kong Sixes? This tournament uses some modified rules due to the use of six-a-side play. Key rules include: Six-a-side teams: Each team sends six players to the field. Six overs per innings: Each team gets a maximum of six overs with six legal balls per over. Bowling: All fielders, excluding the wicket keeper, bowl one over each. A designated player bowls two overs, but not consecutively. Wides and no-balls: They earn one run and an extra ball. There is no free hit for no-balls. Retirement rule: Batting players can retire not out after scoring 50 runs and are allowed back if one of the last two batters gets out. Last-wicket batting rule: If five wickets fall before the six overs are completed, the last batter continues to bat with the fifth batter as the runner. The remaining batter must always face the next delivery. Dismissal of final batter: When the last batter is out; or if the last batter's partner is dismissed through run-out or for obstructing the field, then also the remaining batter is out. The innings ends when the sixth wicket falls. When and where will Hong Kong Sixes 2026 be played? Hong Kong Sixes 2026 will be held between October 30 and November 1 at Tin Kwong Road Recreation Ground in Hong Kong. item.title: Bayern Munich’s Max Eberl confirms Vincent Kompany is still undergoing medical tests, no timeline for return
item.description: (Photo by S. Mellar/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Bayern Munich board member for sport Max Eberl visited head coach Vincent Kompany in the hospital on Saturday, offering some insight into how the head coach is doing following his recent collapse at Säbener Straße. Eberl explained that their conversation had nothing to do with football, with the priority firmly on Kompany’s health and recovery. “I visited Vinnie in hospital on Saturday. We talked about life. We didn’t talk about the Bundesliga or the starting lineup. He’s doing well considering the circumstances. He’s still undergoing tests, but I’m not going to give any updates about that here. We first have to find out exactly what he has, and then let the treatment run. And then when he’s full of energy and healthy again, he will be back,” Eberl said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). Bayern Munich are still waiting for answers as Kompany undergoes further medical examinations, and the club is keeping details of his condition private while doctors work to establish what happened. For now, football takes a back seat. Aaron Danks and the coaching staff will continue handling the team’s preparations, while Kompany focuses on getting healthy. The most important thing is that he makes a full recovery. Bayern Munich will be waiting for him when he is ready to return. Join the conversation! item.title: ‘Is anyone safe?’ – Jonathan Taylor’s wife shares fears about Colts future post Quenton Nelson trade
item.description: Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images Indianapolis Colts RB Jonathan Taylor’s potential trade status has spooked his wife, Ayanna Taylor, after the team traded Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks. A year ago, the Colts were one of the best teams in the NFL, with Taylor looking like an MVP candidate by leading them to an 8-2 season record. Since then, the franchise has gone 2-12 and is 2-5 in the 2026 NFL season. With the team’s playoff hopes all but dead already, the Colts are expected to reshuffle their organisation, already firing team GM Chris Ballard, and now making player trades, making Taylor’s family uncomfortable about what may come next. Jonathan Taylor’s wife thinks Colts might trade them before next week Ayanna Taylor posted a story on Instagram where she is speaking into the camera and sharing her concerns about their future with the Colts after trading away a player like Nelson. “Is literally anyone safe on this team? It feels like rookie year all over again. My mind is spiralling. What does this mean for my husband and I? Do I need to start packing our bags? Are we going to be spending our daughter’s first Halloween together? Will we make it to gameday or was last week the last time my husband is putting on a Colts jersey? What are we going to do without Quenton Nelson?” Nelson was one of the key pieces of the Colts’ defence, and losing him is a visual representation of Indianapolis waving the white flag for this season. Taylor is inarguably their highest-value player. If the Colts are looking for a full organisational reset, moving on from the 27-year-old Taylor for a big haul of draft assets or young players could be their best move to officially embrace the rebuild. Taylor is having a fantastic season, registering 587 yards for eight touchdowns on 140 carries and 178 yards on 17 receptions for a total of 765 yards. Taylor has had multiple 90+-yard rushing games this season, trying to single-handedly spark the Colts’ offence amid struggles from QB Daniel Jones. With Nelson gone and the Colts looking to trade productive players away for future assets, the writing is on the wall for Taylor. However, his age also makes it realistic for the Colts to try and rebuild around him, so a trade away this season does not seem to be set in stone. item.title: AC Milan vs Bologna – Match preview and team news
item.description: AC Milan vs Bologna – Match preview and team news AC Milan and Bologna will face each other on Wednesday at the San Siro in their next Serie A fixture as Ruben Amorim’s men will look for another crucial three points. AC Milan vs Bologna – Match preview and team news Date: Wednesday, 28th October. Kick-off: 5:30pm BST. Venue: San Siro, Milan. AC Milan team news AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim faces a major selection crisis ahead of tonight’s clash, with up to eight first-team players missing or in serious doubt. The biggest blow is Ruben Loftus-Cheek, who is ruled out for a month with a thigh injury sustained against Udinese. He joins Samuel Chukwueze, Mattia Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers, and Filippo Terracciano on the completely sidelined list. Furthermore, Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, and Mario Gila remain major doubts after missing the weekend fixture. With a massive city derby against Inter Milan looming on Saturday, Amorim is highly likely to protect his surviving stars. Veteran midfielder Luka Modrić is expected to be rested on the bench, while talisman Christian Pulisic could also see restricted minutes. In his place, starlet Alphadjo Cissé is heavily tipped to start in the attacking line behind target man Gonçalo Ramos, drastically shifting Milan’s usual tactical shape. Bologna team news Bologna, managed by Raffaele Palladino, arrive at the San Siro in a much healthier position, looking to build on their confident 2-0 victory over Cagliari. The visitors are dealing with only three definitive absences, as star winger Riccardo Orsolini remains out with a hamstring problem, full-back Emil Holm is sidelined, and striker Roberto Piccoli misses out due to a muscular issue. Young forward Jay Enem faces a late fitness check but is unlikely to start. In Piccoli’s absence, Jens Odgaard will continue to spearhead the frontline. Palladino is expected to name former Milan midfielder Tommaso Pobega in the starting lineup alongside Lewis Ferguson to provide steel in central midfield. Additionally, Samuel Mbangula is tipped to replace Nicolò Cambiaghi in the attacking trio, supporting Odgaard alongside Federico Bernardeschi as Bologna aims to exploit a depleted Rossoneri squad. Form AC Milan AC Milan remains one of only four undefeated teams in Serie A this season, boasting five wins and three draws from their opening eight matches. Under Ruben Amorim, their league form is excellent, highlighted by a confident 2-0 away victory over Udinese last Sunday. item.title: Why Casey Woods called Missouri State a 'fighting football team'
item.description: SPRINGFIELD — Missouri State’s heart and soul knew a win wasn’t enough. He wanted to win with style. Linebacker Bird Lloyd and the defense rose to the challenge, holding Sam Houston to zero touchdowns and zero second-half points. Missouri State (3-5, 2-2) earned a gusty 24-3 win to move to .500 in Conference USA play. “Bird said, ‘They are not going to score,’” Casey Woods recalled. “They didn’t.” The Bears delivered a gusty bounce-back performance. Many questions lingered after last week’s disappointing road loss to Delaware. Where Missouri State struggled against the Blue Hens, the Bears quickly cleaned up versus the Bearkats. Missouri State football: Bears earn gutsy win over Sam Houston | Stats, highlights The defense was on a different level, playing its best game of the season. The Bears allowed just 284 yards of offense, the lowest mark against an FBS opponent this season. After giving up 232 rushing yards to Delaware, Missouri State’s rush defense shined against Sam Houston. The Bearkats rushed for 26 yards, a season low for Missouri State. The Bears also sacked Sam Houston’s backup quarterback DJ Bailey five times. Bearkats regular starter Landyn Locke did not feature due to injury. “Our defense played the best game that they’ve played all season,” Woods said. “In eight games, we are a fighting football team. We talked a lot this week about combining effort and execution." The special teams department was enjoying a solid season before the struggles against Delaware. The Bears rose to the occasion, making last week look like an anomaly rather than the norm. Evangel football: Chuck Hepola to retire as coach after season: 'I am deeply grateful' With Missouri State leading 17-3, the Bears punted to the Bearkats with seven minutes remaining. Sam Houston’s Tim Burns Jr. fumbled and Martavis Blackmon secured the fumble. It was the only takeaway of the game for either side and a major turning point. After the fumble, West Plains native Connor Lair scored a short rushing touchdown to ice the game. Blackmon’s individual play made it a decisive moment. “Tonight, I knew I had to just dial in and do my job and play to the whistle, and not after,” Blackmon said. While special teams and the defense bounced back, the offense, led by wide receivers Jmariyae Robinson and Isaiah Myers, couldn’t be slowed. item.content:encoded: SPRINGFIELD — Missouri State’s heart and soul knew a win wasn’t enough. He wanted to win with style. Linebacker Bird Lloyd and the defense rose to the challenge, holding Sam Houston to zero touchdowns and zero second-half points. Missouri State (3-5, 2-2) earned a gusty 24-3 win to move to .500 in Conference USA play. “Bird said, ‘They are not going to score,’” Casey Woods recalled. “They didn’t.” The Bears delivered a gusty bounce-back performance. Many questions lingered after last week’s disappointing road loss to Delaware. Where Missouri State struggled against the Blue Hens, the Bears quickly cleaned up versus the Bearkats. Missouri State football: Bears earn gutsy win over Sam Houston | Stats, highlights The defense was on a different level, playing its best game of the season. The Bears allowed just 284 yards of offense, the lowest mark against an FBS opponent this season. After giving up 232 rushing yards to Delaware, Missouri State’s rush defense shined against Sam Houston. The Bearkats rushed for 26 yards, a season low for Missouri State. The Bears also sacked Sam Houston’s backup quarterback DJ Bailey five times. Bearkats regular starter Landyn Locke did not feature due to injury. “Our defense played the best game that they’ve played all season,” Woods said. “In eight games, we are a fighting football team. We talked a lot this week about combining effort and execution." The special teams department was enjoying a solid season before the struggles against Delaware. The Bears rose to the occasion, making last week look like an anomaly rather than the norm. Evangel football: Chuck Hepola to retire as coach after season: 'I am deeply grateful' With Missouri State leading 17-3, the Bears punted to the Bearkats with seven minutes remaining. Sam Houston’s Tim Burns Jr. fumbled and Martavis Blackmon secured the fumble. It was the only takeaway of the game for either side and a major turning point. After the fumble, West Plains native Connor Lair scored a short rushing touchdown to ice the game. Blackmon’s individual play made it a decisive moment. “Tonight, I knew I had to just dial in and do my job and play to the whistle, and not after,” Blackmon said. While special teams and the defense bounced back, the offense, led by wide receivers Jmariyae Robinson and Isaiah Myers, couldn’t be slowed. The duo is becoming one of Conference USA's best one-two punches. “It’s definitely nice, I love that for us. Defense can’t double one person,” Robinson said. “He’s my yin to my yang.” Quarterback Henry Belin threw a 32-yard touchdown to a wide-open Myers. Sam Houston’s secondary was non-existent in a busted coverage play. Myers literally walked into the end zone near the end of the first quarter. On the first play of the fourth quarter, Missouri State was faced with a 4th-and-2 from Sam Houston’s 37-yard line. Belin dropped back and floated a perfect pass to Robinson for a key touchdown, putting the Bears up 17-3. A great block from Lair in the backfield also set up the play. When asked if he’d rather take Myers’ walk-in touchdown, Robinson smiled and shook his head. “A touchdown is a touchdown,” Robinson responded. The biggest takeaway from Missouri State’s win is its ability to learn from the week before and execute. The Bears accomplished this against Kennesaw State after a road loss to Western Kentucky. Against Sam Houston, the Bears learned from their mistakes versus Delaware. Next week, Missouri State will try to keep the winning ways rolling on the road against FIU. Woods wants to avoid another setback. He wants to keep this team surging forward. “We haven’t played particularly great on the road. We have to respond to that,” Woods said. “Tonight was the best game that we’ve played as a team.” Liam Keating covers high school sports and Missouri State athletics for The Springfield News-Leader. item.title: ‘We all want to put it right’: Man Utd player sends message to fans after confirmation Carrick will be staying put
item.description: ‘We all want to put it right’: Man Utd player sends message to fans after confirmation Carrick will be staying put Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their clash away to Chelsea this Saturday afternoon. One player is said to have told BBC Sport : “The feeling is that we all want to put it right. Players, staff, everyone.” Michael Carrick: The state of play (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) The squad were booed off the pitch at Old Trafford on Sunday following a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth, while Carrick was applauded off and serenaded with his chant from the Stretford End faithful. ESPN has subsequently claimed that fans showing such support for the manager has prompted INEOS to give him the chance to turn things around. However, you’d imagine losses to Chelsea, AS Roma and Aston Villa next weekend would provide them the opportunity to make a managerial change over the November international break. United have now gone eight games without a win, surpassing their previous record of seven winless matches under Louis van Gaal in December 2015. Who could be brought in at Old Trafford? (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) In regard to the options being considered to succeed Carrick, Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are the two favourites, primarily because they are free agents – although INEOS chiefs would reportedly have to pay a £3 million compensation fee to Newcastle United to appoint Howe. Unai Emery has made it clear he’s fully committed to Aston Villa, as has Roberto De Zerbi with Brighton and Hove Albion. Antonio Conte remains an outside candidate, presumably because the board are apprehensive over his managing style and how they could clash heads; the Italian won’t be a yes-man like they’d prefer to employ. After all, it was Ruben Amorim’s public criticism of the hierarchy that led to his premature dismissal last January. Ruben Amorim got a lot wrong. But he worked Manchester United out in a matter of days. Share Tweet Share Share Email Leave a Reply Cancel reply Your email address will not be published. item.title: Bears’ Montez Sweat makes humbling admission on PED suspension
item.description: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Bears’ Montez Sweat makes humbling admission on PED suspension appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Chicago Bears are 5-2 in Ben Johnson’s second season as head coach and are once again looking like playoff contenders in the NFC. However, the Chicago defense has been suspect at times this season, just as it was last year when the Bears lost to the Los Angeles Rams in the Divisional Round. Defensive end Montez Sweat was supposed to be one of the cornerstones of this unit ever since being traded to Chicago back in 2023. However, he has not lived up to that standard and produced the pass-rushing prowess that the Bears had hoped. Then, matters got worse this season when Sweat was suspended for two games due to a PED violation. The Bears went 2-0 without Sweat in the lineup, taking down the Atlanta Falcons and the New England Patriots without him . After that win over New England, Sweat was reinstated. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Heading into Week 8, the standout defensive end made a humbling admission on his suspension. "It was tough. Nobody wants to go look someone in the eye after you've done something detriment like that to the team, but I mean, those are the things you have to do to move forward." Montez Sweat on his conversation with Ben Johnson: ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/7gyZndzoTK — CHGO Bears (@CHGO_Bears) October 27, 2026 “It was tough. Nobody wants to go look someone in the eye after you’ve done something detrimental like that to the team, but I mean, those are the things you have to do to move forward,” Sweat said. Sweat recorded two sacks and two tackles for loss so far this season in five games before the suspension, so the Bears will be hoping for even more production now that he is back. Chicago has a major weakness on the defensive line and has even been floated as a team that could be looking for help in that department at the trade deadline, but getting some strong production from Sweat would certainly help the issue. The Bears have a difficult stretch of schedule coming up, starting with a clash against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks on Monday night in Week 8. Following that one, the Bears will take on the Buccaneers heading into their bye, and taking momentum into the week off will be paramount for Johnson and company as they chase an NFC North title down the stretch of the season. Related: 3 players Bears must target at 2026 NFL trade deadline Related: NFL rumors: Bears fall short in trade pursuits for both Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner. What’s next?

On PP2, Cagnoni led a five-man “swing” entry. 4 left: Couple good looks there for Celebrini line, Graf gets a rebound and had an open net (from some distance), Ellis frozen, but don’t know if Graf shanked it, went wide. Then Misa line follows, Smith negotiates his way up the ice and has a slot shot. Really slow start for the San Jose Sharks, but they picked it up, Buffalo 16-12 shots. Gap was way wider earlier. item.title: Celtics’ Jayson Tatum is finished commenting on Jaylen Brown situation
item.description: Winslow Townson-Imagn Images Celtics’ Jayson Tatum is finished commenting on Jaylen Brown situation appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The trade of Jaylen Brown has already left fans speculating about a deep emotional rift between Jayson Tatum and Brown. Meanwhile, Brown’s recent pointed remark suggested that things might not be entirely smooth between the former teammates. As a result, Tatum once again faced questions about his relationship with Brown, but the Boston Celtics star appears to be done addressing the situation publicly. After the Celtics’ win over the Brooklyn Nets , Tatum was asked about the situation involving Brown, but he made it clear that he had no intention of commenting on the matter any further. “Listen, I said my piece, I’m not making any more comments,” Tatum said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brown was drafted by the Celtics in 2016, while Tatum joined Boston as the third overall pick in 2017. Together, they reached the 2022 and 2024 NBA Finals before ultimately lifting the 2024 NBA championship trophy. Despite their success together, speculation about their chemistry and the Celtics’ direction continued to follow them throughout their time in Boston. Their relationship has always attracted attention because both players are talented scorers. However, after nine seasons together, Boston traded Brown to Philadelphia and chose to build around Tatum. The Celtics cited the financial and roster-building challenges of keeping two players on massive contracts. Reports also suggested that Brown felt disrespected by the organization during his departure. The tension became public after Tatum described how he learned about the trade in a video posted to his YouTube channel. Brown responded to the video with a blue cap emoji. Now, the relationship between Tatum and Brown appears strained by the circumstances surrounding Brown’s exit, though the full extent of any personal disagreement remains unclear. Ultimately, their relationship is more complicated than a simple feud. They achieved significant success together, but the unresolved questions surrounding Brown’s trade have overshadowed their shared legacy. Whether the two can resolve their differences privately remains to be seen. Related: Celtics’ Jayson Tatum isn’t interested in becoming face of Achilles injury Related: Celtics’ Jayson Tatum shares eye-opening take on Derrick White MVP chants

item.title: Brewers blow 12th inning lead, still chasing first World Series title
item.description: Fans at the World Series watch party at American Family field react to Cooper Pratt's go-ahead home run in the 12th inning. (Henry Redman/Wisconsin Examiner) The Milwaukee Brewers came tantalizingly close to winning their first World Series title in franchise history Tuesday evening before the Tampa Bay Rays’ Ben Williamson hit a walk-off single to score the winning run in the bottom of the 12th inning, giving the Rays a 4-3 victory. A Cooper Pratt home run in the top of the 12th inning had the team just three outs away from the championship but a throwing error with zero outs in the top of the inning sparked a rally for the Rays, who for the first time in the series were able to string together a series of hits. Brewers pitcher Shane Drohan, who had previously pitched just one inning in the playoffs, gave up the game tying and winning runs. At American Family Field in Milwaukee a sold out watch party was standing, clapping, cheering and groaning along with the game as if it were happening on the field in front of them and not on the massive screen in center field. The game ended around 11:30, with kids out far past their bedtime and lifelong fans on the edge of their seats to watch their hearts get ripped out. Watching from the third deck was Chrystal Glynn-Skipini who drove down from Neenah to watch the game in the atmosphere with her niece and great nephew. “Why not, how awesome to be with all the other fans,” she said, double crossing her fingers that the team would close out the sweep Tuesday. Game five of the series is Wednesday at 7 p.m. SUBSCRIBE: GET THE MORNING HEADLINES DELIVERED TO YOUR INBOX.

item.title: Celtics superstar Jayson Tatum relishes ‘hell of a feeling’ recording 1st buzzer-beater since Achilles injury
item.description: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images Celtics superstar Jayson Tatum relishes ‘hell of a feeling’ recording 1st buzzer-beater since Achilles injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Boston Celtics superstar Jayson Tatum capped Tuesday night’s 125-124 overtime win over the Brooklyn Nets with his first buzzer-beater since returning from a torn right Achilles, adding another milestone to his comeback. With Boston trailing 124-123 and 2.3 seconds remaining, Derrick White inbounded to Tatum. The Celtics star took two dribbles against rookie Mikel Brown Jr. before burying a 17-foot jumper at the buzzer to seal the team’s third straight victory. Tatum tore his Achilles during the 2025 NBA Playoffs before returning in March. Tuesday marked his first 40-point performance since the injury, while his 18 made free throws on 22 attempts set a career high. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Celtics Wire’s Daniel Donabedian shared Tatum’s postgame reaction on X, formerly Twitter, after Celtics on CLNS’ Noa Dalzell asked how the game-winner felt following his return from injury. Jayson Tatum on hitting his first buzzer-beater since his Achilles injury: “Was a hell of a feeling. Just kind of getting back to doing things that I used to do before I was injured, and sharing that moment with my teammates on the court, seeing them rally and being excited for… pic.twitter.com/8YnwDYemow — Daniel Donabedian (@danield1214) October 28, 2026 Tatum finished with 40 points on 10-of-20 shooting, eight assists and five rebounds while converting a career-high 18 free throws on 22 attempts. Brooklyn forced overtime when Mikel Brown Jr. hit a tying 3-pointer with one second remaining in regulation. The Nets then moved ahead late in the extra period before Tatum answered with the decisive shot. It also marked the third buzzer-beater of the former Duke standout’s NBA career, tying Bill Sharman for third-most in Celtics history behind Paul Pierce and Larry Bird. The Celtics superstar also became the first player in NBA history to record at least 40 points and a game-winning buzzer-beater before November. The victory kept Boston unbeaten at home through its first three games at TD Garden this season while dropping Brooklyn to 0-4. The Celtics improved to 3-1 overall and will host the Chicago Bulls on Friday in NBA Cup action. Related: Celtics’ Jayson Tatum isn’t interested in becoming face of Achilles injury Related: Celtics’ Jayson Tatum shares eye-opening take on Derrick White MVP chants

item.title: A Tale of Two Games: Flyers Start Slow, Followed By Domination, But It Wasn’t Enough
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was a tale of two different games for the Philadelphia Flyers on Tuesday night against the Columbus Blue Jackets. The Blue Jackets got off to a dominant start. Whether that was due to the Flyers’ lack of urgency or complete and utter sloppiness, the Blue Jackets were in the driver’s seat for the first 20 minutes. And it was not even close. Their goals all came in a span of three minutes in the latter half of the first period, but the Blue Jackets put on a clinic. They were dominant along the boards, creating turnovers and keeping most of the first period in their own offensive zone. The Flyers were lifeless, and the Blue Jackets were taking advantage of the Flyers’ mistakes. All of a sudden, it was a 3-0 game after the first period. The Flyers were being outshot 7-2, and things looked mightily bleak. Then, a switch flipped. It’s like the Flyers became a completely different team. After a first period of being outworked, outhustled, and outplayed, it was the Flyers who took a dominant command of the driver’s seat for the final 40 minutes. In periods two and three, the Flyers outshot the Blue Jackets 28-6. They became the team that was controlling play. The pressure was completely flipped, despite the Blue Jackets holding the Flyers to just a goal through 55 minutes of play. Then, with their backs against the wall, the Flyers scored two goals in the final 5 minutes, including Jamie Drysdale ’s equalizer within the final 10 seconds of regulation. They were able to force overtime before their own mistakes once again became costly. It was a tale of two games for the Philadelphia Flyers on Tuesday. One where they were in complete control. The other where they were their own worst enemy. So we’ll take the point, but obviously the start’s got to be better, and it just wasn’t good enough.” The difference between the first 20 minutes and the final 40 was more than significant. It did not just look like two different games. The difference looked like two separate teams. As Sanheim said, there simply was no jump to their game. The Flyers were playing weak and disconnected. They got what was coming to them for their play. Then, the Flyers went into the first intermission and came out of it like a brand new team. They were able to force overtime before their own mistakes once again became costly. It was a tale of two games for the Philadelphia Flyers on Tuesday. One where they were in complete control. The other where they were their own worst enemy. Read More: Flyers Dig Out of First-Period Hole, But Can’t Complete the Comeback in Overtime The Flyers’ Tale of Two Games “Not the start we were looking for,” said Flyers defenseman and alternate captain Travis Sanheim following Tuesday’s 4-3 overtime loss vs. the Blue Jackets . “Didn’t have the energy, and credit to the guys, had the first [intermission] to regroup and find their legs and make it a game. So we’ll take the point, but obviously the start’s got to be better, and it just wasn’t good enough.” The difference between the first 20 minutes and the final 40 was more than significant. It did not just look like two different games. The difference looked like two separate teams. As Sanheim said, there simply was no jump to their game. The Flyers were playing weak and disconnected. They got what was coming to them for their play. Then, the Flyers went into the first intermission and came out of it like a brand new team. The Blue Jackets’ three goals provided a wake-up call for a team that desperately needed one. “I think it took a kick in the butt to get us going ,” said Flyers defenseman Cam York , who made his return to the lineup on Tuesday. “Second and third, we pretty much dominated the game. Just felt like we were on our toes and dictating the pace of play.” Forward Trevor Zegras echoed that message. “We were bad, we weren’t good, we weren’t ready to go. Didn’t get pucks in behind them. Didn’t forecheck. Slow in the zone, taking pucks back, two shots, just not how we play.” But the Flyers’ forward liked the final 40 minutes of regulation. He said then, they looked to the veterans and leaders for a message when they needed it the most. “We kind of looked in the mirror, to our leaders and the veterans, to get us going a little bit, and that’s what we did.” The Flyers had bounced back in a game that felt out of reach after the first period. Then, the mistakes came back to haunt the Flyers in overtime. The Blue Jackets had not one, but two two-on-nones to close out overtime. First, Matvei Michkov was pickpocketed at the blueline, leading to a Cole Sillinger and Zach Werenski rush. Dan Vladar bailed out his forwards, making a showstopping save. However, when it happened again immediately after, the Blue Jackets were bound to score. The Flyers were all trying to pounce on a loose puck in front during 3-on-3. The puck got behind them, and the Blue Jackets beat them to it. When Adam Fantilli and Kent Johnson are leading a rush, the former Wolverine duo is bound to score. “The decision-making in overtime this year has been mind-boggling on some players. We got to fix it quickly ,” said head coach Rick Tocchet on the loss. The Flyers picked up a point. They showed some good, if not great, fight to battle back into the game. The loser point was fought for hard and well earned. But in the end, the start was nowhere near good enough to get them the win, and the overtime was further proof that mistakes remain costly. item.title: Alexander Volkanovski Explains Urgency to Finish Movsar Evloev
item.description: Alexander Volkanovski Movsar Evloev Getty UFC featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski explained why he had so much urgency to finish Movsar Evloev at UFC 333. Volkanovski finished Evloev via second-round TKO in the co-main event of UFC 333 to defend his title for the second time during his second reign as the UFC featherweight champion. It was Volkanovski’s first finish since UFC 290 in July 2023, when he stopped Yair Rodriguez via TKO. Typically, the Aussie is content to outclass his opponents for five rounds and win a decision, but at UFC 333 against Evloev, it seemed clear that a finish was important to him. There is a reason for that. Alexander Volkanovski Explains Why UFC 333 Finish Was So Important Speaking to Brendan Bradford after arriving home in his native Australia, Volkanovski said that getting the finish over Evloev and making sure the fight finished in the second round was so important because he entered the fight with an illness , and he wasn’t confident that he would have his typically strong gas tank had the fight gone the distance. “I’m glad it was only two rounds cuz I was breathing a little heavier than usual. I had to take some big breaths… You could see that I started putting that pressure on, especially in the second round. It was like, alright, let’s start finding this finish. Again, I don’t want to go five rounds. I don’t know if these lungs can hold up being crook (sick) and all. And not only that, I started to see everything and knowing that the finish probably would come,” Volkanovski said (via Bloody Elbow ). Alexander Volkanovski’s Next UFC Challenge After Movsar Evloev Conquered Now that Volkanovski has taken care of the formerly undefeated Evloev, he will take some time off to rest and recover before jumping back into the Octagon in 2027 for his next fight. That could come either in the UFC featherweight division with a title defense against Jean Silva, Aljamain Sterling, or Kevin Vallejos, or Volkanovski may move up to 155 lbs and challenge UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje in what would be a true superfight between two of the sport’s biggest fan favorites. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Alexander Volkanovski Explains Urgency to Finish Movsar Evloev appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: 5 Rays Free Agents Who Will Not Be Coming Back After World Series
item.description: ST PETERSBURG, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 13: Freddy Peralta #51 of the Tampa Bay Rays celebrates after striking out Petey Halpin #0 of the Cleveland Guardians during the sixth inning in game two of the American League Championship Series at Tropicana Field on October 13, 2026 in St Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) Getty The Tampa Bay Rays are trying to defy history and come back from a 3-0 deficit in the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers. They have their work cut out for them as no MLB team has ever come back from a deficit like that in MLB history, so Tampa’s fans must have at least one eye trained on the offseason which will almost certainly see some players currently on the World Series roster depart and join other teams. The Rays are a team that does not like to spend a lot of money on free agents and they avoid overpaying for players whose value will probably not be worth a pricey free agent contract. That’s why these five players seem almost certain to depart after the World Series no matter what the result is. Rays can say goodbye to these 5 free agents after this season Freddy Peralta Tampa Bay decided to be uncharacteristically aggressive at the trade deadline and swung a blockbuster deal with the New York Mets for right-handed ace Freddy Peralta. The front office knew this team was special and given how weak the American League was this season, president of baseball operations Erik Neander made a wise risk to go out and get one of the best starting pitchers available. While Peralta really struggled with the Mets to the tune of a 4.99 ERA, the change of scenery did wonders for him as he posted a 3.25 ERA in 10 regular season starts with the Rays. He also pitched well in the playoffs, but the sad fact is that he’s just going to be too expensive for the Rays. Expect one of the big-market teams to sign him. Nick Martinez Another starting pitcher who is likely to be gone is Nick Martinez. The Rays opted to have him start Game 1 of the World Series and he had a really great season. He had a 15-6 record and a 3.10 ERA in 31 starts. He made his first All-Star Game and ironically may have pitched his way out of Tampa Bay’s price range for next season. He has a $20 million mutual option for next season but he may decide to opt out of his deal and test free agency thinking he could potentially earn more on the market. If he does, the Rays seem highly unlikely to outbid another team so odds are he will not be coming back after the World Series. Gavin Lux Acquired by Tampa Bay Rays ahead of the 2026 season, Gavin Lux hasn’t played for months due to an injury. He only played in the minors for the Rays this season and hit a forgettable .223/.387/.298 with one homer and 12 runs batted in across 28 Triple-A games. He is clearly on the decline and there is no reason for the Rays to bring him back unless it is on a minor league deal where he’d have to earn his way back to the big leagues. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) Getty The Tampa Bay Rays are trying to defy history and come back from a 3-0 deficit in the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers. They have their work cut out for them as no MLB team has ever come back from a deficit like that in MLB history, so Tampa’s fans must have at least one eye trained on the offseason which will almost certainly see some players currently on the World Series roster depart and join other teams. He had a 15-6 record and a 3.10 ERA in 31 starts. He made his first All-Star Game and ironically may have pitched his way out of Tampa Bay’s price range for next season. He has a $20 million mutual option for next season but he may decide to opt out of his deal and test free agency thinking he could potentially earn more on the market. If he does, the Rays seem highly unlikely to outbid another team so odds are he will not be coming back after the World Series. Gavin Lux Acquired by Tampa Bay Rays ahead of the 2026 season, Gavin Lux hasn’t played for months due to an injury. He only played in the minors for the Rays this season and hit a forgettable .223/.387/.298 with one homer and 12 runs batted in across 28 Triple-A games. He is clearly on the decline and there is no reason for the Rays to bring him back unless it is on a minor league deal where he’d have to earn his way back to the big leagues. He was once a promising young player for the Los Angeles Dodgers but that feels like ages ago now. Jorge Mateo The Rays scooped up shortstop Jorge Mateo after he was let go by the Atlanta Braves midseason. He was not productive at all with the Rays, hitting a disappointing .141/.181/.205 with one homer and seven runs driven in across 32 games. Like Lux, it would only make sense to bring him back on a minor league deal but Mateo will likely ty to test the market and see if he can get a deal with a club that will give him a chance to make the big-league club. Austin Slater Outfielder Austin Slater bounced around from team to team in 2026. He was once a mainstay with the San Francisco Giants as a platoon bat who killed lefties, but he just has not been able to stick with any club in recent seasons. He didn’t do terribly for the Rays, hitting .273/.360/.364 in 25 plate appearances, but he didn’t make enough of an impression for Tampa to be highly incentivized to bring him back so expect him to try to join yet another team in the offseason. The Rays make logical, practical decisions in free agency so if a player does not provide much value or if their market value is not in accordance with the actual value they are likely to produce on the field then they are going to stay far away from them. One might think they’d be more aggressive after a World Series appearance, but they got to the World Series by being disciplined so expect them to continue with that approach. item.title: Lekkerimäki Scores Twice, Canucks Snap 10-Game Losing Streak In 6-5 Overtime Win Against Anaheim
item.description: In a surprising turn of events, the Vancouver Canucks overcame a 5–2 deficit to take a 6–5 win in overtime against the Anaheim Ducks tonight. Jonathan Lekkerimäki led the way in scoring for the Canucks with two tallies in the final three minutes of the game, while Liam Öhgren, Brock Boeser, Jamie Oleksiak, and Filip Hronek also found the back of the net. Leevi Meriläinen was solid in net once again, stopping 18 of 23 shots faced. The Canucks’ offensive woes persisted during the first period, though by no means were they as lacking as they have been in previous matchups. While it took Vancouver a little less than eight minutes to record their first shot on goal of the game, after that, the Canucks were able to put together a decent run of O-zone time. Anaheim’s first goal of the game came off a performance of individual skill from Ducks forward A.J. Greer as well as a bad-luck play for Hronek. Cutting into Vancouver’s zone, Greer spun to evade the check of defenceman Elias Pettersson before deftly throwing the puck on net. At the same time, Hronek, chasing down a netfront-bound Tim Walshe, wound up in the unfortunate position that allowed the puck to bounce off him and past Meriläinen. A solid start to the second period saw Öhgren tie the game up for Vancouver after some strong spells of offence for the Canucks. However, just like how they have on other occasions this season — and twice in this particular game — Vancouver surrendered a goal from the Ducks very soon after tying the game up. The Ducks’ goal count snowballed from there, with Vancouver exiting the second frame down 4–1. The Ducks’ fourth goal in particular saw yet another unlucky bounce play against Vancouver’s favour. Just as a puck bounced off Hronek and in during the first period, so did the puck that ultimately resulted in a goal for Leo Carlsson. After Meriläinen made the save off a rush chance for Anaheim, the puck rebounded off Zeev Buium’s skate, redirecting into the prime position for Carlsson to shoot it into a yawning Canucks cage. Vancouver fired up their engines once the third period started up. While Boeser’s goal was soon followed by yet another Ducks goal for Greer, the Canucks weren’t done quite yet. Oleksiak answered Anaheim’s goal with one of his own, bringing the score to 5–3. Down two goals with less than four minutes to go in regulation, Vancouver’s coaching staff made a bold move by putting four forwards and one defenceman out on the ice before pulling Meriläinen and adding yet another forward on the ice. The play seemed to work, however, as Lekkerimäki tickled the twine twice to tie things up, using Jake DeBrusk as a screen for both. Overtime saw the Canucks put together a string of chances before Lekkerimäki drew a high-sticking call on Beckett Sennecke while maintaining control over the puck. item.content:encoded: In a surprising turn of events, the Vancouver Canucks overcame a 5–2 deficit to take a 6–5 win in overtime against the Anaheim Ducks tonight. Jonathan Lekkerimäki led the way in scoring for the Canucks with two tallies in the final three minutes of the game, while Liam Öhgren, Brock Boeser, Jamie Oleksiak, and Filip Hronek also found the back of the net. Leevi Meriläinen was solid in net once again, stopping 18 of 23 shots faced. The Canucks’ offensive woes persisted during the first period, though by no means were they as lacking as they have been in previous matchups. While it took Vancouver a little less than eight minutes to record their first shot on goal of the game, after that, the Canucks were able to put together a decent run of O-zone time. Anaheim’s first goal of the game came off a performance of individual skill from Ducks forward A.J. Greer as well as a bad-luck play for Hronek. Cutting into Vancouver’s zone, Greer spun to evade the check of defenceman Elias Pettersson before deftly throwing the puck on net. At the same time, Hronek, chasing down a netfront-bound Tim Walshe, wound up in the unfortunate position that allowed the puck to bounce off him and past Meriläinen. A solid start to the second period saw Öhgren tie the game up for Vancouver after some strong spells of offence for the Canucks. However, just like how they have on other occasions this season — and twice in this particular game — Vancouver surrendered a goal from the Ducks very soon after tying the game up. The Ducks’ goal count snowballed from there, with Vancouver exiting the second frame down 4–1. The Ducks’ fourth goal in particular saw yet another unlucky bounce play against Vancouver’s favour. Just as a puck bounced off Hronek and in during the first period, so did the puck that ultimately resulted in a goal for Leo Carlsson. After Meriläinen made the save off a rush chance for Anaheim, the puck rebounded off Zeev Buium’s skate, redirecting into the prime position for Carlsson to shoot it into a yawning Canucks cage. Vancouver fired up their engines once the third period started up. While Boeser’s goal was soon followed by yet another Ducks goal for Greer, the Canucks weren’t done quite yet. Oleksiak answered Anaheim’s goal with one of his own, bringing the score to 5–3. Down two goals with less than four minutes to go in regulation, Vancouver’s coaching staff made a bold move by putting four forwards and one defenceman out on the ice before pulling Meriläinen and adding yet another forward on the ice. The play seemed to work, however, as Lekkerimäki tickled the twine twice to tie things up, using Jake DeBrusk as a screen for both. Overtime saw the Canucks put together a string of chances before Lekkerimäki drew a high-sticking call on Beckett Sennecke while maintaining control over the puck. Anaheim went down by two players later on after Alex Killorn collided with Meriläinen, giving Vancouver a golden opportunity to end the game in overtime — which is exactly what Hronek did by firing the puck after a series of passes in the O-zone. "When you string together as many losses as we have, it bleeds into the room, and then the morale obviously takes a hit. So not just getting a win, but a big come-from-behind win in the third is obviously something that we can build off of," said Canucks Head Coach Manny Malhotra post-game. Overall, tonight was a good character win for the Canucks. Yes, they do still have some things to clean up, such as their shifts following a goal-for and their power play (which went 0-for-4 in full power plays prior to overtime), but given the streak they just snapped, Vancouver is likely happy with tonight's effort. item.title: Knicks’ Mike Brown reveals challenge to Karl-Anthony Towns at halftime vs. Pistons
item.description: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Knicks’ Mike Brown reveals challenge to Karl-Anthony Towns at halftime vs. Pistons appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Karl-Anthony Towns led the New York Knicks to their first win of the season on Tuesday, as they beat the Detroit Pistons, 111-97, at Madison Square Garden. Towns tallied a double-double of 27 points and 20 rebounds on top of three assists. He shot 12-of-21 from the field. While he had seven turnovers, his activity on both ends helped the Knicks snap their three-game losing skid. In the postgame conference, coach Mike Brown gave credit to Towns and revealed that he issued a challenge to the 30-year-old center at halftime. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “KAT is a grown man. He’s obviously a perennial All-Star. I just told him the truth: ‘KAT, the guy (Paul Reed) is killing us on the glass, and when he gets a rebound, he’s putting it back, or anything he gets in the paint, he’s putting it back. If he gets on the perimeter, guard him. He did those things,” said Brown in the video posted by SNY. “I gotta take my hat off to KAT because I thought his shift in his mindset was really big for us in the second half.” Mike Brown said he challenged Karl-Anthony Towns after halftime "I just told him the truth. 'KAT, [Paul Reed] is killing us on the glass and when he gets a rebound he's putting it back. If he gets on the perimeter, guard him. And he did those things" pic.twitter.com/IpGB5ESpdT — SNY Knicks (@sny_knicks) October 28, 2026 The Knicks outscored the Pistons, 37-13, in the third quarter. Detroit rallied in the fourth quarter, but New York, which led by as much as 27 points, had enough of a cushion to fend it off. Towns said he did not want to disappoint the home crowd , stressing the need to give them something to cheer about after their 0-3 start. The six-time All-Star had plenty of support, with Jalen Brunson adding 23 points and seven rebounds and OG Anunoby tallying 13 points, seven rebounds, two steals, and two blocks. Related: Knicks’ Jalen Brunson reveals what fuels Josh Hart’s ‘different’ mindset Related: Knicks’ Karl-Anthony Towns reveals what it took to lock in defensively vs. Pistons
