item.title: 3 Takeaways as Wembanyama and the Spurs get right vs. Sacramento Kings
item.description: Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) dunks the ball during the NBA game against the Sacramento Kings at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) The oldest player on the Spurs' active roster went zipping through the lane in garbage time Tuesday, soaring for a surprising dunk that got everyone else on the bench up and cheering. Harrison Barnes' out-of-nowhere slam not only put the finishing touches on the Spurs' 130-103 demolition of the woeful Sacramento Kings at the Frost Bank Center. It also drew the appreciation of one Victor Wembanyama. "I stood up so quick I started getting dizzy," Wembanyama said. Having slogged through a sluggish 1-2 start to the season, the defending Western Conference champs discovered the best way to get back to feeling like themselves. It involves scheduling the Sacramento Kings. Wembanyama went for 29 points, 10 rebounds and four blocks, Julian Champagnie supplied eight 3-pointers and 26 points off the bench and the Spurs rolled to their most lopsided win of the season. "Every game has gotten a little bit better," said coach Mitch Johnson, whose team has won two in a row after beginning 0-2. "I thought they came to play tonight." Give the 0-4 Kings credit for being a willing participant of their own demise. Domantas Sabonis tallied 20 points and 14 rebounds, DeAndre Hunter scored 24 and Zach LaVine chipped in 22. None of that was remotely enough to get the Kings within sniffing distance of their first victory of the season. The Spurs led 80-54 at half and by as many as 27 points in the second half. Scoreboard aside, the Spurs were most interested in their own improvement. Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) celebrates a win during the NBA game against the Sacramento Kings at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) "Whether the ball is going through the hoop or not, our standard stays the same," Champagnie said. "We came out and did exactly what we were supposed to do. We played exactly how we want to play." Here are three takeaways from Tuesday's victory, which evened the Spurs' record at 2-2 heading into a Wednesday showdown at Utah: 1. Wembanyama enjoys a dunk-a-thon Throughout an up-and-down start to the season for Wembanyama, Spurs coaches and teammates have talked about the need to make their All-Star center's life easier on the offensive end. One number summed up how successful the Spurs were in that endeavor Tuesday. Nine. Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) dunks the ball during the NBA game against the Sacramento Kings at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) That's how many dunks Wembanyama registered against the Kings, equaling a career single-game high. For comparison, the 7-foot-4 center had totaled 10 dunks in his first three games. Within the first 2:19 Tuesday, Wembanyama had scored a pa
item.content:encoded: Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) dunks the ball during the NBA game against the Sacramento Kings at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) The oldest player on the Spurs' active roster went zipping through the lane in garbage time Tuesday, soaring for a surprising dunk that got everyone else on the bench up and cheering. Harrison Barnes' out-of-nowhere slam not only put the finishing touches on the Spurs' 130-103 demolition of the woeful Sacramento Kings at the Frost Bank Center. It also drew the appreciation of one Victor Wembanyama. "I stood up so quick I started getting dizzy," Wembanyama said. Having slogged through a sluggish 1-2 start to the season, the defending Western Conference champs discovered the best way to get back to feeling like themselves. It involves scheduling the Sacramento Kings. Wembanyama went for 29 points, 10 rebounds and four blocks, Julian Champagnie supplied eight 3-pointers and 26 points off the bench and the Spurs rolled to their most lopsided win of the season. "Every game has gotten a little bit better," said coach Mitch Johnson, whose team has won two in a row after beginning 0-2. "I thought they came to play tonight." Give the 0-4 Kings credit for being a willing participant of their own demise. Domantas Sabonis tallied 20 points and 14 rebounds, DeAndre Hunter scored 24 and Zach LaVine chipped in 22. None of that was remotely enough to get the Kings within sniffing distance of their first victory of the season. The Spurs led 80-54 at half and by as many as 27 points in the second half. Scoreboard aside, the Spurs were most interested in their own improvement. Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) celebrates a win during the NBA game against the Sacramento Kings at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) "Whether the ball is going through the hoop or not, our standard stays the same," Champagnie said. "We came out and did exactly what we were supposed to do. We played exactly how we want to play." Here are three takeaways from Tuesday's victory, which evened the Spurs' record at 2-2 heading into a Wednesday showdown at Utah: 1. Wembanyama enjoys a dunk-a-thon Throughout an up-and-down start to the season for Wembanyama, Spurs coaches and teammates have talked about the need to make their All-Star center's life easier on the offensive end. One number summed up how successful the Spurs were in that endeavor Tuesday. Nine. Spurs center Victor Wembanyama (1) dunks the ball during the NBA game against the Sacramento Kings at Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026. (Andrew J. Whitaker/San Antonio Express-News) That's how many dunks Wembanyama registered against the Kings, equaling a career single-game high. For comparison, the 7-foot-4 center had totaled 10 dunks in his first three games. Within the first 2:19 Tuesday, Wembanyama had scored a pair of baskets on lob passes from De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle. To hear Wembanyama tell it, the Spurs would love to start every game this way. "We always try to do it," Wembanyama said. "It's the most efficient shot in the game." That idea doesn't always work out well. It did Tuesday. Wemby on all of his lob dunks versus the Kings https://t.co/rMdHz8Nl3s - Spurs Nation (@Spurs_Nation) October 28, 2026 In all, 24 of Wembanyama's 29 points against Sacramento came at the rim. It was a far cry from Wembanyama's previous performance at the Frost Bank Center, when he went a career-worst 1-of-13 from the field in the Spurs' season-opening loss to Oklahoma City. How did the Spurs make Wembanyama's life easier? "Better spacing, cleaner execution, he continued to roll and trust it and allow his teammates to make him better at times," Johnson said. "And on the other end they rewarded him in that." 2. Champagnie threatens own 3-point mark By halftime Tuesday, Champagnie had turned in a curious box score. Eight made 3-pointers. Two airballs. "Hey listen," Champagnie said. "I'll take eight makes and two airballs." Champagnie six 3-pointers during a sizzling second quarter tied a Spurs record. His eight 3-pointers in the first half, meanwhile, matched his own record set last New Year's Eve against New York. His teammates kept finding him for open looks. He kept knocking them down. Julian Champagnie had a big night from 3. Why? He says it's his teammates. Also he believes in heat checks … https://t.co/CSjnQqRaYp - Spurs Nation (@Spurs_Nation) October 28, 2026 By game's end, Champagnie couldn't quite reach the lofty heights he did that night against the Knicks, when he finished with a club-record 11 3-pointers. He went 1 of 3 from beyond the arc in the second half Tuesday to finish 8 of 13. It was all part of the Spurs' best 3-point shooting night of the season, as they made 17 of 37 from long range. Through the first three games, Johnson maintained that the team's process for generating clean shots beyond the arc remained sound. The Spurs just weren't hitting enough of them. That all changed Tuesday, with the Spurs' shooters followed Champagnie's lead. 3. Rookie guard keeps firing for Kings Sacramento rookie Darius Acuff Jr. entered Tuesday chasing a record of his own. Whether that was a good thing or bad thing is in the eye of the beholder. Acuff, selected 7 th overall in the June draft, came into the contest having launched 73 field-goal attempts, the most in NBA history for a first-year player in his first three games. The previous mark of 64 was set by Kevin Durant in 2006-07, when he played for Seattle. Before the game, Kings coach Doug Christie described Acuff as "unflappable" and "the ultimate competitor." "He's not ducking anything, that's for sure," Christie said. Acuff got up another 20 shot attempts against the Spurs, extending his own record for most 20-shot games to open a career to four. There are those in NBA circles who question the wisdom of letting a rookie get his feet wet in league by shot chucking. Acuff's heavy shot diet hasn't exactly resulted in wins for the Kings. He has not been the paragon of efficiency, either. The 19-year-old guard went 8 of 20 on Tuesday for 19 points, bringing his season shooting percentage to 32.9%. It is already shaping up to be a long season in Sacramento. Acuff could provide plenty of highlights. It is worth wondering whether the shot-heavy approach the Kings are pushing will hinder the youngster's growth. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. This article originally published at 3 Takeaways as Wembanyama and the Spurs get right vs. Sacramento Kings .

item.title: Rays avoid World Series sweep, edge Brewers in extra-innings Game 4
item.description: Tampa Bay Rays players celebrate after Ben Williamson hit a walk-off RBI single in the bottom of the 12th inning of a 4-3 win over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the 2026 World Series on Wednesday at Tropicana Field in St Petersburg, Fla. Photo by Aaron Josefczyk/UPI Oct. 28 (UPI) -- Ben Williamson slammed a sinker into the dirt and over the infield for a dramatic walk-off single, completing a Game 4 rally past the Milwaukee Brewers and extending the 2026 World Series on Wednesday in St. Petersburg, Fla. Williamson's game-winning hit came in the bottom of the 12th inning of the 4-3 triumph, which started Tuesday and ended after midnight at Tropicana Field. With the win, the Rays forced a Game 5 and denied the Brewers of becoming the first team to sweep their final two best-of-seven-game series en route to a title. "It just shows the resiliency of this group," said Williamson, who was 1 for 15 this postseason before his pinch-hit, game-winning single. "We continue to fight." Game 5 will be held Wednesday in St. Petersburg. The Brewers, who remain one win away from their first title, rallied from two deficits in Game 4. Rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt hit a go-ahead homer in the top of the 12th, but the Rays responded by reaching base safely five consecutive times to start the bottom of the inning. Tampa Bay Rays pinch hitter Ben Williamson hits an RBI single in the bottom of the 12th inning of a win over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the 2026 World Series on Wednesday at Tropicana Field in St Petersburg, Fla. Photo by Aaron Josefczyk/UPI Center fielder Jonny DeLuca tied the score with an RBI single. Williamson ended the game two at-bats later, plating pinch runner Nick Fortes when he hit the first pitch he saw from relief pitcher Shane Drohan to right field. "We are going to keep fighting until the end," said Rays left fielder Chandler Simpson, who went 3 for 5 in the win. Tampa Bay Rays pinch runner Nick Fortes scores the winning run after Ben Williamson hit an RBI single in the bottom of the 12th inning of a win over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the 2026 World Series on Wednesday at Tropicana Field in St Petersburg, Fla. Photo by Aaron Josefczyk/UPI Simpson plated Game 4's first run with an RBI double in the second. Pratt tied the score with an RBI double in the fourth, but the Rays regained the lead off a throwing error in the bottom of the frame. Brewers third baseman David Hamilton led off the fifth with his second homer of the postseason. That 391-foot solo shot tied the score at 2-2. Tampa Bay Rays players hug Ben Williamson after he hit an RBI single in the bottom of the 12th inning of a win over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the 2026 World Series on Wednesday at Tropicana Field in St Petersburg, Fla. Photo by Aaron Josefczyk/UPI Center fielder Jonny DeLuca tied the score with an RBI single. Williamson ended the game two at-bats later, plating pinch runner Nick Fortes when he hit the first pitch he saw from relief pitcher Shane Drohan to right field. "We are going to keep fighting until the end," said Rays left fielder Chandler Simpson, who went 3 for 5 in the win. Tampa Bay Rays pinch runner Nick Fortes scores the winning run after Ben Williamson hit an RBI single in the bottom of the 12th inning of a win over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the 2026 World Series on Wednesday at Tropicana Field in St Petersburg, Fla. Photo by Aaron Josefczyk/UPI Simpson plated Game 4's first run with an RBI double in the second. Pratt tied the score with an RBI double in the fourth, but the Rays regained the lead off a throwing error in the bottom of the frame. Brewers third baseman David Hamilton led off the fifth with his second homer of the postseason. That 391-foot solo shot tied the score at 2-2. Tampa Bay Rays players hug Ben Williamson after he hit an RBI single in the bottom of the 12th inning of a win over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the 2026 World Series on Wednesday at Tropicana Field in St Petersburg, Fla. Photo by Aaron Josefczyk/UPI Both teams continued to threaten, but did not score over the next four frames, forcing extra innings. Neither team recorded a hit in the first two extra frames. Pratt then settled in against relief pitcher Ian Seymour to start the 12th. He proceeded to smack a 2-2 Seymour sweeper over the left field fence for his first playoff home run. Rays third baseman Junior Caminero reached on a fielding error to lead off the bottom of the final inning. Catcher Liam Hicks, DeLuca, Simpson and Williamson connected for singles over the game's final four at-bats to extend the Rays' season. Tampa Bay Rays starting pitcher Griffin Jax throws against the Milwaukee Brewers in the first inning of a win over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the 2026 World Series on Tuesday at Tropicana Field in St Petersburg, Fla. Photo by Aaron Josefczyk/UPI Rays starter Griffin Jax allowed four hits and two runs over four innings. The Rays bullpen surrendered just four hits and one run over the final eight. Brewers starter Dustin May allowed three hits and two runs over three innings. Brewers relief pitcher Aaron Ashby, who did not allow a hit over 2 1/3 innings, set a record for the most consecutive scoreless innings in a single postseason, with 18. Tampa Bay Rays center fielder Jonny DeLuca celebrates after hitting a game-tying RBI single against the Milwaukee Brewers in the 12th inning of Game 4 of the 2026 World Series on Tuesday at Tropicana Field in St Petersburg, Fla. Photo by Aaron Josefczyk/UPI Hicks went 2 for 5 in the win. Designated hitter Yandy Diaz, who went 1 for 4 with a walk, joined Simpson and Hicks as the only Rays players to reach base more than once in Game 4. Pratt went 4 for 5 with two RBIs and a run scored. His Brewers teammates went a combined 4 for 38 in the loss. Left fielder Jackson Chourio, who went 2 for 6, tied Babe Ruth's 1928 record for the the most hits through four games of a World Series, with 10. The Rays (1-3) will host the Brewers (3-1) in Game 5 at 8 p.m. EDT Wednesday in St. Petersburg.

item.title: Sauk Rapids ends season vs. Bemidji behind 4 touchdowns from Halverson
item.description: SAUK RAPIDS, Minn. — As Bemidji’s senior running back Garret Halverson found the edge and accelerated towards the pylon midway through the third quarter to take a commanding two-score lead, it became clear to most surrounding the Sauk Rapids Middle School field that the final varsity game played on the grounds would be one in defeat as the Lumberjacks held on for a 35-21 victory in the Section 8AAAAA Quarterfinals. More: Albany volleyball starts quest for Section 6AA three-peat with win vs. Cathedral More: St. Cloud-area football teams get MSHSL sectional drawings. See the matchups “There’s a lot of history here,” Sauk Rapids head coach Phillip Klaphake said. “There’s been a lot of winning [on this field]. This place has meant a lot to our community for a really long time; it’s been an awesome place. I’ve been fortunate enough to get to coach here for over 10 years now, and I have had some really cool experiences here.” The Storm have seen sectional champions and state tournament teams call the field home over the last three decades and close the final chapter on the field with an unfortunate loss to Bemidji. It is the Lumberjacks first win of the season and the first for head coach Kyle McMartin. “We’ve been preaching on these kids that if they can do the things right, success will come to them and to not quit,” McMartin said. “We told them this whole week that our record is 0-0; it was really nice to see them actually pull through.” Bemidji leaned heavily on Halverson throughout the night as the senior back stacked up four rushing touchdowns against the Storm. Senior ATH Owen Vandermeer had the lone score for the Lumberjacks that did not belong to Halverson, finding the endzone on an end around at the end of the first half to make it a 14-13 deficit. Halverson quickly got touchdowns No. 2 and 3 after a three-and-out and an interception ended the Storm’s first two drives of the second half. “Our O-Line stepped up in a big way,” McMartin said. “Garrett has been doing a heck of a job; we put an emphasis on breaking the first tackle and just continuing to punish people. The kid runs hard every single play and every single down. We’re really proud of him and what he’s done for himself.” With the win, the Lumberjacks will be heading to Section 8AAAAA No. 1 Brainerd to play on Saturday, Oct. 31. item.title: 'He is selfless!': Abhishek Sharma credits Sanju Samson for setting India's fearless tone
item.description: 'He is selfless!': Abhishek Sharma credits Sanju Samson for setting India's fearless tone originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Abhishek Sharma hit 113 off 38 balls as India chased 199 in Wellington against New Zealand. Sanju Samson gave up his opening slot and moved down to number three. Abhishek called it selfless, as it let Vaibhav Sooryavanshi open in his usual spot. Abhishek Sharma praises Sanju Samson's 'selfless' character after helping India clinch the T20I series against New Zealand Abhishek Sharma has described Sanju Samson as “selfless” after India’s thumping win in Wellington, and the opener made it clear that the sacrifice his teammate made in the batting order was a big reason why the side could play with such freedom. On Tuesday, India reached a target of 199 in only 13.2 overs, and they went about it as though it were a routine chase. Abhishek brought up his fifty in 15 balls, moved to his fourth T20I century in 35 balls and finished on 113 off 38 deliveries. He also managed to take the spotlight away from Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who was batting superbly at the other end. The two of them added 133 for the first wicket in just 7.1 overs, and India raced to 118 without loss in the powerplay, which is a T20I record. MORE: India’s batting belief is reaching frightening levels However, to understand what Abhishek meant, it helps to look at how India’s batting order has changed through the series. In the first T20I in Christchurch, Samson and Abhishek opened the innings, with Tilak Varma coming in at number three. Samson set the tone in a chase of 226 with 67 off 33 balls and was named Player of the Match. Kishan then picked up an injury and missed the second T20I, so Sooryavanshi was brought in at number three, while Samson and Abhishek continued as the opening pair. The order was reshuffled for the third match. Abhishek and Sooryavanshi opened, which is the role the young left-hander usually plays, and Samson, who has done well at the top and mostly bats there, was demoted to number three. He gave up a place he has made his own, purely for the sake of the team combination. Speaking at the presentation and then to the media, Abhishek moved the attention away from his century and onto what Samson had done for the group. He said the whole dressing room had picked up on it, and that it had made the afternoon easier for everybody who went out to bat. “We opened today, Sanju bhai opens first, we can see that everyone in the team is selfless. I feel that the atmosphere that the team showed today, it will be easy for everyone,” he said. He then pointed to Samson’s innings in the earlier matches and explained how willingly the senior batter had accepted a different role in the lineup. “Like Sanju bhai played his innings in the last 2 matches, I feel everyone, someone is going at his position like Sanju bhai showed his character, I feel whole team did," he added. MORE: Bhuvn

Abhishek Sharma praises Sanju Samson's 'selfless' character after helping India clinch the T20I series against New Zealand Abhishek Sharma has described Sanju Samson as “selfless” after India’s thumping win in Wellington, and the opener made it clear that the sacrifice his teammate made in the batting order was a big reason why the side could play with such freedom. On Tuesday, India reached a target of 199 in only 13.2 overs, and they went about it as though it were a routine chase. Abhishek brought up his fifty in 15 balls, moved to his fourth T20I century in 35 balls and finished on 113 off 38 deliveries. He also managed to take the spotlight away from Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who was batting superbly at the other end. The two of them added 133 for the first wicket in just 7.1 overs, and India raced to 118 without loss in the powerplay, which is a T20I record. MORE: India’s batting belief is reaching frightening levels However, to understand what Abhishek meant, it helps to look at how India’s batting order has changed through the series. In the first T20I in Christchurch, Samson and Abhishek opened the innings, with Tilak Varma coming in at number three. Samson set the tone in a chase of 226 with 67 off 33 balls and was named Player of the Match. Kishan then picked up an injury and missed the second T20I, so Sooryavanshi was brought in at number three, while Samson and Abhishek continued as the opening pair. The order was reshuffled for the third match. Abhishek and Sooryavanshi opened, which is the role the young left-hander usually plays, and Samson, who has done well at the top and mostly bats there, was demoted to number three. He gave up a place he has made his own, purely for the sake of the team combination. Speaking at the presentation and then to the media, Abhishek moved the attention away from his century and onto what Samson had done for the group. He said the whole dressing room had picked up on it, and that it had made the afternoon easier for everybody who went out to bat. “We opened today, Sanju bhai opens first, we can see that everyone in the team is selfless. I feel that the atmosphere that the team showed today, it will be easy for everyone,” he said. He then pointed to Samson’s innings in the earlier matches and explained how willingly the senior batter had accepted a different role in the lineup. “Like Sanju bhai played his innings in the last 2 matches, I feel everyone, someone is going at his position like Sanju bhai showed his character, I feel whole team did," he added. MORE: Bhuvneshwar Kumar's India return disappoints, but there's no need to panic yet BCCI/Creimas Gautam Gambhir’s fearless culture: strike rate first, personal milestones second Samson’s willingness to move down fits neatly with the approach that has taken hold in this India side. Every batter walking out appears to follow a strike-rate-first plan, which is meant to “kill the game in the Powerplay itself”, a line of thinking that Samson himself had stressed earlier. Abhishek was able to make use of the risk-taking licence that the dressing room had already built up. Indian cricket has often been criticised from outside for batters who pile up individual numbers. Abhishek’s tribute, though, shows how the leadership group, under head coach Gautam Gambhir, has made it normal to give up personal statistics for the team’s run rate. The respect between Abhishek and Samson also stands out, because they could easily have been rivals for the same slot, but they back each other’s attacking style instead. MORE: Illegal combo: Fans react as Abhishek-Sooryavanshi blitz through 199-run chase Samson’s sacrifice is the quiet story behind India’s fearless batting The record powerplay and the 35-ball hundred will rightly fill the headlines, but the more telling moment came after the match, when Abhishek chose to thank a teammate. Samson had scored heavily at the top of the order, had won a Player of the Match award in the series opener, and had every reason to expect that he would keep his place there. Instead, he accepted a move to number three without any fuss, so that Sooryavanshi could open in the position where he is most comfortable. That kind of decision rarely gets the credit it deserves. Batters build their careers on the opening slot, and giving it up, even for one game, can feel like a step backwards. Samson saw it as a way to help the combination work, and the result on Tuesday spoke for itself. It also sends a message to the rest of the squad. When a senior player is ready to change his role for the team’s benefit, nobody else can reasonably complain about their own place in the order. That sort of trust is hard to create and easy to lose, and Gambhir and the leadership group will want to protect it as the series moves on. If the dressing room keeps thinking this way, India’s fearless approach will stay very difficult for any opposition to counter. item.title: Brewers rookie Cooper Pratt stuns Rays with late home run in World Series Game 4
item.description: Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Brewers rookie Cooper Pratt stuns Rays with late home run in World Series Game 4 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It may have taken until the top of the 12th inning, but the Milwaukee Brewers have finally broken the deadlock in Game 4 of the World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays. Leading off the inning against reliever Ian Seymour, rookie Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt just had the biggest hit of his life by going yard to give Milwaukee a 3-2 lead in extras. COOPER PRATT WITH THE BIGGEST HOME RUN OF HIS CAREER 😤 BREWERS LEAD 3-2 IN THE 12TH!! pic.twitter.com/aoSX6iMXnT Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 28, 2026 It was a hanging 2-2 curveball that Pratt sent to deep left field for his first career postseason home run. And there’s no better time for the rookie shortstop to come up huge for the Brewers, as they only need to get three more outs to win the franchise’s first World Series title. Pratt has been on fire on the night, with that clutch long ball in the 12th being his fourth hit of the night in five at-bats. The Brewers have seemingly gotten every clutch hit whenever they needed it, and now, they’re on the cusp of winning it all. In Game 2, it was Sal Frelick , he of the four regular-season long balls, who hit the go-ahead home run to complete the comeback for Milwaukee. And now, Pratt, who only hit three dingers in the regular season in 74 games, has become the latest unlikely hero for Milwaukee. It wasn’t that long ago when Pratt was in the minor leagues; it wasn’t even that long ago when Pratt drew the ire of manager Pat Murphy for purportedly failing to hustle on a few plays, which ended up getting him benched. But now, Pratt has become a true Brewers legend, which should especially be the case if Milwaukee finishes the game by shutting the door in the bottom of the 12th. At only 22 years of age, Pratt has done something most big-leaguers could only dream of, and it’s going to be incredible to see how much better he can be as he goes deeper into his career. Related: Brewers’ Pat Murphy reveals why he kept Jacob Misiorowski out of World Series Game 4 Related: 3 Brewers to blame for missed World Series sweep chance in Game 4 vs. Rays

item.title: Minicucci starts 18/18, throws for 414, and leads Delaware to 35-21 victory at WKU
item.description: CHARLOTTESVILLE, VA - SEPTEMBER 26: Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens quarterback Nick Minicucci (4) scrambles out of the pocket during a college football game between the Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens and the Virginia Cavaliers on September 26, 2026, at Scott Stadium in Charlottesville, VA. (Photo by Lee Coleman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It was Minicucci Mania on Tuesday night in Bowling Green, KY. Delaware quarterback Nick Minicucci missed the Fightin’ Blue Hens’ first two conference games with a lower body injury, and the team went 0-2 without its star. Last week, Minicucci returned with a leg brace and guided Delaware to 61 points behind a program record five touchdowns passes. In his second game back, he continued to rewrite Delaware’s record books. Minicucci set the Delaware record for most consecutive completions, starting the game a perfect 18-of-18. He finished an efficient 32-of-38, throwing for 414 yards (sixth-most in program history) and four touchdowns without an interception, leading the Fightin’ Blue Hens to a 35-21 road win over Western Kentucky. The game started out as the ultimate offensive fireworks show. The first three drives all resulted in touchdowns. Then after an exchange of turnovers within a three-play span, the offenses got back to work and three more touchdowns were scored. Delaware and WKU were knotted at 21-21 by the 7:25 mark of the second quarter. Tuesday night’s showcase also offered an incredibly rare spectacle — there was not a single incompletion in the first 33 passes. Minicucci started 18-of-18, while WKU quarterback Brock Glenn started 14-of-15, tossing an interception to Delaware strong safety Kevin Moore late in the first quarter. The first pass that hit the turf transpired with 1:44 remaining in the first half when Minicucci finally snapped his historic 18-of-18 start. He was the first CUSA quarterback to start 18-of-18 since former Midddle Tennessee quarterback Brent Stockstill on Sept. 3, 2016. However, Minicucci responded to that first incompletion with three-straight completions, traveling 25, 34, and 8 yards. The 8-yard completion went to running back Jo Silver for a go-ahead touchdown with 59 seconds remaining in the second quarter, providing Delaware with its first lead, 28-21. The second half contrasted greatly from the first. There were only seven points scored when Delaware claimed a 35-21 lead with 4:20 left in the third quarter on a 40-yard strike from Minicucci to Sean Wilson. Otherwise, the half featured four punts, two missed field goals, an interception, and four turnovers on downs (three by WKU). While Minicucci remained efficient in the second half, Glenn’s completion percentage tailed off as Delaware’s defense forced the WKU quarterback to finish 25-of-37. Free safety AJ Graham recorded a second interception for the Fightin’ Blue Hens, while defensive end Trace Scott III produced two of Delaware’s three sacks Tuesday night. Wilson was another standou
item.content:encoded: CHARLOTTESVILLE, VA - SEPTEMBER 26: Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens quarterback Nick Minicucci (4) scrambles out of the pocket during a college football game between the Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens and the Virginia Cavaliers on September 26, 2026, at Scott Stadium in Charlottesville, VA. (Photo by Lee Coleman/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It was Minicucci Mania on Tuesday night in Bowling Green, KY. Delaware quarterback Nick Minicucci missed the Fightin’ Blue Hens’ first two conference games with a lower body injury, and the team went 0-2 without its star. Delaware and WKU were knotted at 21-21 by the 7:25 mark of the second quarter. Tuesday night’s showcase also offered an incredibly rare spectacle — there was not a single incompletion in the first 33 passes. Minicucci started 18-of-18, while WKU quarterback Brock Glenn started 14-of-15, tossing an interception to Delaware strong safety Kevin Moore late in the first quarter. The first pass that hit the turf transpired with 1:44 remaining in the first half when Minicucci finally snapped his historic 18-of-18 start. He was the first CUSA quarterback to start 18-of-18 since former Midddle Tennessee quarterback Brent Stockstill on Sept. 3, 2016. However, Minicucci responded to that first incompletion with three-straight completions, traveling 25, 34, and 8 yards. The 8-yard completion went to running back Jo Silver for a go-ahead touchdown with 59 seconds remaining in the second quarter, providing Delaware with its first lead, 28-21. The second half contrasted greatly from the first. There were only seven points scored when Delaware claimed a 35-21 lead with 4:20 left in the third quarter on a 40-yard strike from Minicucci to Sean Wilson. Otherwise, the half featured four punts, two missed field goals, an interception, and four turnovers on downs (three by WKU). While Minicucci remained efficient in the second half, Glenn’s completion percentage tailed off as Delaware’s defense forced the WKU quarterback to finish 25-of-37. Free safety AJ Graham recorded a second interception for the Fightin’ Blue Hens, while defensive end Trace Scott III produced two of Delaware’s three sacks Tuesday night. Wilson was another standout performer for Delaware, and the wide receiver finished with nine receptions for 183 yards and two touchdowns, with a longest reception of 40 yards — nearly duplicating his Week 3 stat-line of nine receptions for 185 yards and two touchdowns, with a longest reception of 40 yards against Coastal Carolina. Wilson also produced the viral moment of the game. After scoring the game-tying touchdown in the second quarter, he went face-to-face with WKU’s iconic mascot Big Red, engaging in some player to mascot trash talk. Big Red of Western Kentucky pressing a Delaware WR after a touchdown is the most Tuesday night college football thing ever pic.twitter.com/K87mCWOA3o — Aidan Doc 🧸 (@AidanDoc__) October 27, 2026 😤 pic.twitter.com/PLRznRvYAE — Delaware Football (@Delaware_FB) October 27, 2026 WKU (3-5, 2-2 CUSA) snaps its two-game win streak and drops its first home game of the season. The Hilltoppers will have nearly two weeks to recover, as they resume action Nov. 7 at Middle Tennessee for the 100 Miles of Hate rivalry. Delaware (4-4, 2-2 CUSA) reverted to .500 with its star quarterback in the lineup. The Fightin’ Blue Hens are 4-0 this year, and 2-0 in CUSA play, when Minicucci has been available throughout the entire game. Minicucci will receive additional recovery time as Delaware also takes the field next Nov. 7 when it visits Kennesaw State.

item.title: How Rays' stunning 12th-inning rally denied Brewers' bid for World Series sweep
item.description: How Rays' stunning 12th-inning rally denied Brewers' bid for World Series sweep originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Baseball's future after the World Series is uncertain as a lockout approaches. Baseball's present is wildly entertaining. The Rays ensured that the World Series will go to a fifth game for a 14th consecutive season with a win on Tuesday night, but it wasn't an ordinary win. Tampa Bay was down to its final three outs in the bottom of the 12th inning, when an error sparked an offense that was dormant for most of the night. A Brewers offense that got nothing but outs in the later innings suddenly couldn't get an out, and the chance to win a championship was denied for at least one night. Here's a look at the anatomy of the Rays' 12th-inning comeback. MORE: How Brewers built World Series team with low budget Rays' 12th-inning rally vs. Brewers The Rays struggled to put anyone on base in the later innings as the Brewers used the full force of their bullpen to try to close out a championship. Against all odds, Tampa Bay outlasted it. By the 12th inning, the Brewers had to turn to Shane Drohan, who just didn't have it. A throwing error by Joey Ortiz allowed Junior Caminero to reach base against Antonio Senzatela, who was then lifted by Pat Murphy. That appeared to be the plan all along. Joey Ortiz bounces a throw that Jake Bauers couldn't scoop to begin the bottom of the 12th inning https://t.co/jwjqSaBMw9 — Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) October 28, 2026 Tasked with getting the final three outs of the World Series, Drohan got none. The Rays went single, single, single, single, starting with a hit by Liam Hicks that sent a hobbled Caminero to third base. Jonny DeLuca, who came up short in a game-ending at-bat earlier in this series, then chopped one up the middle to tie the game. JONNY DELUCA TIES THE GAME IN THE 12TH! https://t.co/Urc9nwUt67 — MLB (@MLB) October 28, 2026 Chandler Simpson kept the line moving, as he does best, and loaded the bases for Ben Williamson with no outs. With the game extended and the pressure now significantly reduced, Williamson chopped one into right field for the win, without the Brewers ever recording an out. BEN WILLIAMSON WALK-OFF RAYS SURVIVE! https://t.co/bjHolx3L4m — MLB (@MLB) October 28, 2026 The roles were suddenly reversed in this series, with the Brewers experiencing a bullpen meltdown and the Rays small-balling their way into a rally. Whether it goes down as the start of something special or a brief moment of relief for the Rays is still to be determined, but a win on Wednesday would already make Tampa Bay the first team in World Series history to force a Game 6 after falling behind 3-0. To do it, they will have to get by Jacob Misiorowski. MORE MLB: Brewers fans amaze with takeover of Tropicana Field 5 big things to know about impending MLB lockout Ranking the top 16 MLB free agents

item.title: ‘Is He Dissing (LeBron James)?’ ‘Fried (Deandre) Ayton’ — NBA Fans Read Between the Lines As Austin Reaves Praises New-Look Lakers’ Lack of ‘Egos’
item.description: 'Is He Dissing (LeBron James)?' 'Fried (Deandre) Ayton' -- NBA Fans Read Between the Lines As Austin Reaves Praises New-Look Lakers' Lack of 'Egos' The Los Angeles Lakers are off to a 3-0 start, and Austin Reaves believes their lack of egos is helping the team get results. But when Reaves praised the group’s willingness to embrace their roles, NBA fans had different ideas about who he might have had in mind. Some wondered whether the guard was taking a subtle shot at LeBron James, who left Los Angeles for the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency. Others believed the comments had more to do with Deandre Ayton, whose short Lakers stint ended with a trade to the Washington Wizards. NBA Fans Debate Who Austin Reaves Meant by ‘No Egos’ Remark Reaves offered his thoughts after the Lakers erased an 18-point deficit to beat the Utah Jazz 132-123 on Sunday. With James gone, Reaves has taken on an even bigger role alongside Luka Dončić, serving as the team’s secondary scorer and a key playmaker. When discussing the team’s chemistry, Reaves credited the players with understanding their responsibilities and putting winning first, per Spectrum SportsNet. “We have a team that understands roles and what is asked of them to do,” Reaves explained . “And if they’re gonna do everything that we ask them to do, you gotta help them in situations. I think the beautiful thing about our team is there’s no egos, there’s no anything. You just wanna win basketball games, and however that happens is the main thing.” DON’T MISS: ‘He Just Dropped 47,’ ‘Depression’ — Hoops World Reels From ‘Awful’ Anthony Edwards Injury News As Timberwolves Star Faces Months-Long Absence Reaves did not mention James or compare the current locker room with previous Lakers teams. Still, the comments quickly sparked speculation online. One NBA fan wondered whether the guard was taking aim at his former teammate, asking , “Is he dissing bron ? Bet.” Another fan took the speculation further, declaring , “They really hated the tf outta Bron lmfao.” However, others pushed back against the idea that James was the target. One fan argued , “Trolls mentioning Bron are ignored this obviously about Ayton.” Another defended Reaves’ relationship with the four-time NBA champion, adding , “Reaves loves LeBron so I’m not gonna entertain trolls lmao.” A separate fan was equally dismissive of the James angle, writing , “This isn’t about Bron lol.” Lakers Lead also stepped in to defend Reaves, warning against reading too much into the comments : “Incoming comments thinking this is sneak dissing bron. If u know ANYTHING about Austin Reaves he has the ultimate respect for LeBron.” Some fans, however, pointed to a different target: Ayton, the Lakers’ former center. Los Angeles signed Ayton in July 2025 to address its need for size and rim protection. However, his lone season (2025-26) with the team fell short of expectations. He averaged a career low of 12.5 points per game before the Lakers traded him to Washington in J

You just wanna win basketball games, and however that happens is the main thing.” DON’T MISS: ‘He Just Dropped 47,’ ‘Depression’ — Hoops World Reels From ‘Awful’ Anthony Edwards Injury News As Timberwolves Star Faces Months-Long Absence Reaves did not mention James or compare the current locker room with previous Lakers teams. Still, the comments quickly sparked speculation online. One NBA fan wondered whether the guard was taking aim at his former teammate, asking , “Is he dissing bron ? Bet.” Another fan took the speculation further, declaring , “They really hated the tf outta Bron lmfao.” However, others pushed back against the idea that James was the target. One fan argued , “Trolls mentioning Bron are ignored this obviously about Ayton.” Another defended Reaves’ relationship with the four-time NBA champion, adding , “Reaves loves LeBron so I’m not gonna entertain trolls lmao.” A separate fan was equally dismissive of the James angle, writing , “This isn’t about Bron lol.” Lakers Lead also stepped in to defend Reaves, warning against reading too much into the comments : “Incoming comments thinking this is sneak dissing bron. If u know ANYTHING about Austin Reaves he has the ultimate respect for LeBron.” Some fans, however, pointed to a different target: Ayton, the Lakers’ former center. Los Angeles signed Ayton in July 2025 to address its need for size and rim protection. However, his lone season (2025-26) with the team fell short of expectations. He averaged a career low of 12.5 points per game before the Lakers traded him to Washington in July 2026 for guard Jaden Hardy and two future second-round picks (2031, 2032). One NBA observer bluntly put it , “Fried Ayton.” Another offered a harsher assessment of his time in Los Angeles, quipping , “The Ayton experience was miserable for everyone lmao.” A separate commenter also leaned toward Ayton rather than James as the likely reference, explaining , “People saying Bron but Ayton was the first name that popped up for me. Feel like LeBron did a good job accepting a secondary role last season.” For now, Reaves has not clarified whether he had anyone specific in mind. With the Lakers unbeaten so far, their early results are giving them plenty to celebrate. Whether the team’s improved chemistry has anything to do with either James’ or Ayton’s exit, however, remains unconfirmed. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Conor McGregor’s Coach Reveals His Mentality After Injury Against Max Holloway
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - JULY 11: Conor McGregor of Ireland looks on prior to facing Max Holloway of the United States in their welterweight bout during UFC 329 at T-Mobile Arena on July 11, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) Getty Conor McGregor‘s coach, John Kavanagh, revealed how his pupil came to terms with his injury against Max Holloway. McGregor sustained a knee injury during the opening exchange of his main event bout at UFC 329. What made the former two-division UFC champion’s injury more devastating is that it transpired during his comeback fight. McGregor’s fight against Holloway marked his first appearance after breaking his leg during his bout against Dustin Poirier five years earlier. Kavanagh revealed that while McGregor was disappointed, he was actively inquiring about potential next steps. “You’re in that rollercoaster of emotion, you’re just a bit all over the place. Right away, [McGregor] was talking about ‘Well, what’s the surgery options? What’s the recovery time like?’ I think from doing his ACL to fighting, he’s done in the past in nine months – from injury to returning to the octagon,” Kavanagh told The Ariel Helwani Show . Kavanagh also noted that McGregor was spending time with his family, which he feels put him at ease. “I thought that was great for Conor as well that he had his brain being kept busy with family stuff as much as he could, entertaining the kids and just getting on with it. There’s no point in dwelling on it,” Kavanagh said. John Kavanagh Believes Conor McGregor Will Make UFC Another Comeback John Kavanagh also spoke about Conor McGregor’s fighting future and expressed his belief that his pupil will return to the octagon. Kavanagh revealed that McGregor has been aggressive with his recovery and seems to be on the right track. “[McGregor] says he does [fight again]. I’m just too long around him – I think we’re now 22 years around each other – and I’ve just seen him do too many things that seem to be impossible. And he does them repeatedly. So, if he says he does [fight again], I’m not gonna doubt him,” Kavanagh told The Ariel Helwani Show . “He’s going through his rehab now, and, he’s back. He looks pretty good to me, he looks to be moving around quite well. So, he’s been very aggressive with his therapy and his recovery. And then I guess we wait to see what happens next year,” Kavanagh said. Kavanagh Optimistic About McGregor’s Recovery Kavanagh remains optimistic that McGregor will make another UFC comeback and is not concerned about the Irishman’s age. McGregor will be 39 years old by the time he is expected to be cleared to return. While McGregor’s age may be a cause for concern, Kavanagh pointed to advancements in sports medicine. As long as the Irishman stays committed to his training, Kavanagh feels his pupil will pursue another fight. “[McGregor’s] always said, and it is now with nutrition and the approach to strength and conditioning, athletes’ lifespan is certainly extending.

item.title: 'Shut the hell up: Charles Barkley sends message to Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown amid 'beef'
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images Everybody has had an opinion on the ongoing drama between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown, and Charles Barkley has now weighed in on the situation. The championship-winning duo at the Boston Celtics seemed to have a great relationship at one point, but that has turned sour in recent months. Both players have had their say publicly, but Barkley seems to be tired of their feud already. Charles Barkley tells Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown to shut up and play basketball Brown commented a ‘cap’ emoji under a video of Tatum saying he actually had no idea that the latter was being traded by the Celtics. Then, when the Boston star claimed that he had no ‘beef’, Brown responded by saying there could be some lamb chops and gravy. It’s clear that the feud between the two players has not been settled yet, and that seems to be bothering Barkley, who has had a go at both of them. He said on SiriusXM’s NBA Radio : “I think both of them are really good players and both of them are good dudes. You can’t feed this machine, man, because every time you say something, the media, the internet, they’re going to take it to a whole other level. “Okay, they won a championship together. I think they’re both good dudes and they’re both hell of players. Just shut the hell up and play basketball. It’s over. “I think Jayson tried to, like, ‘hey man, I got no beef with JB.’ And JB’s like, well, ‘no beef, it’s like some chicken and some gravy.’ I’m like, yo, man, what are we (doing here)? “It’s like, y’all both are grown a** men. Y’all both great basketball players. The relationship is over. Come on. That kind of stuff always bothers me. I’m not going to lie. Come on, man.” Tatum must have heard Barkley and everyone else’s opinions on this drama, as after the Celtics’ dramatic win over the Nets, he refused to further fuel the drama with Brown. “Listen, I’ve said my piece. I’m not making any more comments on this,” he said in his press conference. It remains to be seen now if Brown will put an end to this situation as well. item.title: Fantastic Fleetwood seal shootout success in Carabao Cup shock against Arsenal
item.description: It is more than 20 years since Arsenal played at Highbury but their trip to League Two Fleetwood – and a stadium of the same name – did not bring back fond memories as they were dumped out of the Carabao Cup on penalties. It was the team with red shirts and white sleeves that triumphed, but on this occasion it caused one of the greatest upsets in English football history. Aaron Loupalo-Bi and Viktor Gyökeres exchanged goals in normal time but Arsenal were unable to find a winner, despite being the dominant force, as Fleetwood battled to the end. The home manager, Matt Lawlor, was almost in tears, unable to cope after the tension was released when Conor Haughey smashed the ball into the top corner to settle the shootout. Continue reading...

item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Alexia Putellas a worthy Ballon d’Or winner but the limited shortlist illustrates flaws
item.description: Neglect of African football and a third win for the Spanish great does little to challenge narrative that the prize is reserved only for top nations’ players After a four-year wait, Alexia Putellas is the queen of women’s football once again. Receiving the Ballon d’Or for a record‑equalling third time to continue Spain’s domination of the award, the 32-year-old reinforces her status as one of the greatest players of all time. It was the sixth consecutive year in which the honour went to either Putellas or her international teammate Aitana Bonmatí, and it was symbolic of Putellas’s resurgence after her comeback from the anterior cruciate ligament injury she sustained in 2022, her refusal to surrender her career to that setback, and her majestic rise back to the top. Continue reading...

item.title: Kylian Mbappé apologises after being dropped by Chinese brands for Mao Zedong comment
item.description: Video appears to show Mao Zedong called a ‘dictator’ Dongpeng and Mengniu end deals with the player Kylian Mbappé has apologised after the Real Madrid forward was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with the state-run Chinese digital newspaper The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappé saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photoshopped on to that of “some guy – I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappé superimposed on an image of Mao. Continue reading...

item.title: England Under-15s walk off pitch against Ireland in World Cup after racism allegation
item.description: Match in new Fifa competition abandoned England players refuse to resume match England abandoned their Under-15 World Cup match against the Republic of Ireland on Monday after a player reported being subjected to a racist slur. Fifa confirmed it was investigating what happened in the final minute of the Group C fixture in Baku, Azerbaijan, when Ireland were leading 4-1. Footage showed an England player approaching the bench after an altercation. He is believed to have alleged an opponent called him a “monkey” and raised a complaint with the coaching staff, prompting England’s head coach, Matt Thorpe, to approach the referee. item.title: Damning data: stats that show Michael Carrick’s luck was bound to run out | Andrew Beasley
item.description: Favourable conditions and the rub of the green were behind Manchester United’s successful finish to last season Manchester United have been the third‑best team in the Premier League with Michael Carrick as their head coach. It is some effort for his job to be so under threat when only Arsenal (57 points) and Manchester City (56) have been more productive than United (46) during the 45-year-old’s tenure. The tally obscures pertinent facts. United topping the Premier League during his 17‑match interim spell last season is irrelevant when they sit 16th with no win in eight games in all competitions this season. Losing narrowly against City is one thing, but three-goal defeats by Como and Bournemouth will surely spell managerial change. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Russo to Arsenal’s rescue and Olid makes Manchester United progress
item.description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. Suzanne Wrack Continue reading...

item.title: McTominay stars in Napoli draw that leaves Allegri ‘not lucid enough’ to talk | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Gli Azzurri show positive signs of improvement in seesaw 3-3 draw against a Roma side inspired by Messi-like Matías Soulé Scott McTominay was leaving nothing to doubt. He appeared to have scored with a close-range header early in the second half of Napoli’s game at home to Roma, but Pierluigi Gollini clawed the ball out from inside the goal. McTominay got his noggin to the rebound, nudging it back across the line. Roma’s keeper pushed away again, so the Napoli midfielder got to his feet and smashed the loose ball into the back of the net. Just typical. You wait two months for your first goal of the Serie A season, then three show up at once. They only counted for one, of course, but McTominay looked happy enough with that as he ran to thank Matteo Politano for the assist. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Bournemouth’s transfer nous puts United to shame, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa The three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

item.title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager
item.description: Sage’s side beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle ‘Every mistake that is bad will be a goal’ Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.” Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Mamdani loves Arsenal. He should challenge them to cut ties with the UAE over Sudan | Sasha Lezhnev and John Prendergast
item.description: The New York mayor’s passion for the Gunners and human rights presents an opportunity to push back on the club’s lucrative UAE sponsorship Like him or not, there is no doubt that New York mayor Zohran Mamdani’s passion for certain issues is electric, and that passion played a large part in him getting elected. But today, two of his biggest passions are on a collision course. On one hand, Mamdani is now arguably the US’s most high-profile supporter of English Premier League champions Arsenal. A superfan since he was a child , he has put the Gunners into the American spotlight more than anyone since becoming mayor. The Empire State Building gleamed in Arsenal’s red and white when they won the Premier League title. He wrote an essay about what Arsenal’s championship means to him, talks about Arsenal at press conferences and interviews and inaugurated Thierry Henry Way near Times Square in honor of the Arsenal legend. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. Niall McVeigh Ipswich v Nottingham Forest, Friday 8pm BST Aston Villa v Manchester City, Saturday 12.30pm BST Arsenal v Everton, Saturday 3pm BST Coventry v Fulham, Saturday 3pm BST Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: John Brewin
item.content:encoded: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: pressure mounts on Slegers as Hemp closes on record
item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. In contrast, Birmingham scored with their one shot on target as Océane Hurtré took her impressive tally to six in six. Sophie Downey Match report: Arsenal 1-1 Birmingham Continue reading...

item.title: Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One
item.description: Gary Caldwell, club captain in 2013 and now manager, needs much more than the weekend win against Reading to disperse the clouds If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern‑day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win against Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...

Written mainly by Júlia Belas Trindade and Sophie Downey , expect guest appearances from stars such as Anita Asante, Ada Hegerberg and many more.
